definition_zh: 演示；报告；赠予；颁发；呈现方式；首演
definition_en: a talk in which someone shows and explains something to an audience; also the act of giving something formally, the way something appears, or a first public performance
core_image: 讲台前的人把图表转向观众，手指停在最关键的一行
scene: 会议室的灯暗下来，投影亮起，讲者把第一张图表转向台下，手指停在最关键的一行。Her presentation on water reuse lasted twenty minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 presentation 指「演示、报告」（第 1 个义项：面向听众讲解并展示内容）；句意为她关于水循环利用的演示持续了二十分钟。图中可辨识物件：投影幕、图表、讲台。

derivatives.zh: 由 present 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「演示者；主持人」
由 present 加 -able 构成，义为「拿得出手的；像样的」
由 presentation 加 -al 构成，义为「呈现方式的；与展示有关的」

senses.title: A talk that shows and explains something
senses.definition: a formal talk in which someone shows and explains a subject to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 面向听众展示并讲解某一主题的正式讲话
senses.example: She gave a clear presentation on water reuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她就水的循环利用作了一场清晰的报告。
senses.why: The word is built from a Latin verb meaning to place something before someone, so the earliest image is an object set in front of the eyes, which is exactly what a talk with slides does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个拉丁动词，意思是「把东西放到某人面前」，所以最早的画面是把物件摆到眼前给人看；带幻灯片的报告做的正是这件事，于是「演示」成为最贴近原意的义项。

senses.title: The act of giving something formally
senses.definition: a formal ceremony or act in which something is given to someone
senses.definitionCN: 把某物正式交给某人的仪式或行为
senses.example: The presentation of the prize took place at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖仪式在中午举行。
senses.why: If presenting is placing something in front of a person, the same gesture covers handing a gift or an award into someone's hands, so the verb of showing becomes a noun of giving.
senses.whyCN: 既然「呈现」是把东西放到人面前，那么把礼物或奖章交到对方手上也是同一个动作，于是表示「展示」的词自然分出「赠予、颁发」这一义。

senses.title: The way something appears or is shown
senses.definition: the way in which something is shown, arranged, or appears to others
senses.definitionCN: 某物被展示、安排或呈现给他人的方式
senses.example: The presentation of the data matters as much as the data.
senses.exampleCN: 数据的呈现方式和数据本身同样重要。
senses.why: Once the word names the act of putting something before the eyes, it can also name the resulting look, because what the audience sees is the arrangement itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指「把东西摆到眼前」这个动作，它也能指摆好之后的样子，因为观众看到的正是那个安排方式，所以词义从「动作」滑到「呈现出来的形态」。

senses.title: A first public performance
senses.definition: the first public performance of a play, film, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或音乐作品首次公开演出
senses.example: The new opera had its presentation in Vienna.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新歌剧在维也纳首演。
senses.why: A performance puts a work before an audience for the first time, which is the same placing-before gesture, so the word extends from showing an object to showing a whole work.
senses.whyCN: 演出就是把一部作品第一次摆到观众面前，仍是「置于人前」的手势，所以词义从展示一件物品扩展到展示一整部作品，专指首演。

intro.en: Presentation comes from a Latin verb for placing something before someone; the noun names that placing, and English spread it from showing to giving and performing.
intro.cn: presentation 来自表示「把东西放到某人面前」的拉丁动词；名词指这一摆放动作，英语再把它从展示扩展到赠予与演出。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it marks whatever is set ahead of something else.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，标示被放在别的东西之前。

items.en: The verb esse meant to be, and its present participle praesens described what is here and in front of someone.
items.cn: 动词 esse 意为「存在、是」，它的现在分词 praesens 指「在场的、在某人面前的」。

items.en: Praesentare turned that adjective into a verb: to bring something into someone's presence, to place it before the eyes.
items.cn: praesentare 把这个形容词变成动词：把东西带到某人面前，摆到眼前。

items.en: The noun praesentatio named the act of placing or showing, and it passed into Old French as presentation with the same sense.
items.cn: 名词 praesentatio 指「摆放、展示」这一行为，进入古法语后写作 presentation，含义不变。

items.en: English took the French noun as presentation and widened it to talks, awards, visible forms, and first performances.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入 presentation，并把词义扩展到报告、颁奖、呈现形态与首演。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin adjective for being present and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of public talk and display.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「在场」的拉丁形容词及其英语词族展开；近义组收其他公开讲话与陈列展示的说法。

entries.definition: The verb and adjective at the base of presentation: to show or give, or being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: presentation 的动词与形容词基础形式：展示、赠送，或「在场的」。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place or near someone.
entries.definitionCN: 在场；存在；出席。

entries.definition: A person who gives a presentation or hosts a show.
entries.definitionCN: 作演示的人；节目主持人。

entries.definition: Tidy enough to be shown or offered to others.
entries.definitionCN: 拿得出手的；像样的。

entries.definition: A formal talk given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。

entries.definition: An educational talk, usually to students.
entries.definitionCN: 通常面向学生的教学讲座。

entries.definition: A practical showing of how something works.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物如何运作的示范。

entries.definition: An arrangement of things put out for people to see.
entries.definitionCN: 把物品摆出来供人观看的陈列。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin act of placing something before someone, dressed with an English noun ending; its family returns again and again to showing and handing over.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「把东西放到人前」的动作，加上英语名词后缀；同族词反复回到展示与交出。

normal.en: Presentation is present plus -ation: present means placing something before someone, and -ation names the act, so the word is literally the act of placing before.
normal.cn: presentation 是 present 加 -ation：present 指把东西放到人面前，-ation 命名这个动作，所以字面就是「摆到人前」这件事。

normal.en: Presenter swaps -ation for -er, turning the act into the person who performs it.
normal.cn: presenter 把 -ation 换成 -er，把动作变成做这个动作的人。

normal.en: Presentable keeps the -able ending: something that can be presented, that is fit to be shown.
normal.cn: presentable 保留 -able，表示「可以被呈现的」，也就是拿得出手的。

normal.en: Presence and presentation share the same Latin adjective praesens, which describes what is here in front of you.
normal.cn: presence 与 presentation 共用同一个拉丁形容词 praesens，都描述「就在你眼前」的东西。

normal.en: The award sense survives in phrases like the presentation of prizes, where the act of handing over is still a public placing before the crowd.
normal.cn: 「颁发」这一义仍活在 the presentation of prizes 一类说法里：把东西交出去，仍是在众人面前的一次公开摆放。

abstract.en: Every presentation moves something invisible, an idea or a claim, into the space in front of other people.
abstract.cn: 每一场演示都把看不见的东西——一个想法或一个主张——搬进别人眼前的空间。

abstract.en: The same word covers a slide talk and a medal ceremony because both put an object where eyes can reach it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指幻灯片报告又指颁奖，因为两者都是把东西放到目光够得着的地方。

abstract.en: To present is to accept that a thing is judged by how it is placed, not only by what it is.
abstract.cn: 去呈现，就是承认一件事会被按照「摆放的方式」来评判，而不只看它本身是什么。

examples.en: The presentation lasted twenty minutes and ended with questions.
examples.cn: 这场演示持续了二十分钟，最后以提问结束。

examples.en: The presentation of the awards began at noon.
examples.cn: 颁奖仪式在中午开始。

examples.en: His calm presentation of the facts convinced the room.
examples.cn: 他对事实的冷静呈现说服了在场所有人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞森特申」——把东西「送到」大家面前，就是演示与颁发；谐音只帮记忆，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在，现在分词 praesens「在场的」）→ praesentare（摆到面前）→ 拉丁名词 praesentatio → 古法语 presentation → 英语 presentation；核心是「把东西置于人前」。

sensesIntro.en: The core act is placing something before someone; the senses divide into a public talk, a formal handover, a visible form, and a first performance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是「把东西摆到人前」；义项由此分为公开报告、正式交付、可见形态与首次演出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker turning a chart toward the audience and stopping a finger on the key line.
core.cn: 核心意象：讲者把图表转向听众，手指停在最关键的一行。

branches.en: a slide turning toward the audience
branches.cn: 幻灯片转向听众

branches.en: a speaker pausing on the key figure
branches.cn: 讲者在关键数字上停顿

branches.en: a medal placed in a waiting hand
branches.cn: 奖章放进等候的手心

branches.en: the same facts arranged two different ways
branches.cn: 同样的事实被排成两种样子

branches.en: a curtain rising on a first night
branches.cn: 首演之夜拉开的幕布

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin prefix of place, a Latin verb of being, the verb that means to place before, and the noun and English endings built on them.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「存在」的拉丁动词、表示「摆到前面」的动词，以及其上的名词与英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: being present, in front of someone
to show or give; a gift

definition_zh: 不久；很快；目前；现在
definition_en: after a short time; also at the present time or moment
core_image: 一个人站在站台边看表，说再等一会儿就出发，而此刻他还站在原地
scene: 火车站的广播刚响过，朋友还没到，他看了看表，对电话那头说再等一会儿就好。The train will leave presently, so stay near the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 presently 指「不久、很快」（第 1 个义项：在很短时间之后）；句意为列车很快就要开了，所以别走远。图中可辨识物件：站台、时钟、行李箱。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 praesens 进入英语的形容词，义为「现在的；出席的」，是 presently 的词干
由拉丁 praesentia 进入英语，义为「在场；出席」，与 presently 同源
由 present 与 day 复合而成，义为「当今的；当前的」

senses.title: After a short time
senses.definition: at a time not long from now, or soon after a point in the past
senses.definitionCN: 在离现在不远的将来，或在过去某一时点之后不久
senses.example: The doctor will see you presently.
senses.exampleCN: 医生很快就会给你看诊。
senses.why: The base word describes what is here and now, and the -ly ending turns that nearness into a point just ahead of now, so the word points to a moment slightly in front of the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 词干描述「就在眼前、就在此刻」，-ly 把这种贴近感变成一个时间点：事情已经贴近眼前，发生的时刻就在稍前一点，于是产生「不久、很快」的用法，重心落在说话之后的短时间里。

senses.title: At the present time
senses.definition: at this moment or during the current period
senses.definitionCN: 在此刻或当前这段时期
senses.example: The office is presently closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室目前因维修关闭。
senses.why: Because present already means what exists now, the adverb can simply stand for at this time, and this reading has become the dominant one in modern American usage.
senses.whyCN: present 本身就指「此刻存在的」，副词直接取其「现在」一义即可；现代美式英语里这个读法已经压过「不久」，成为最常用的理解，所以同一拼写要按上下文分辨。

intro.en: Presently is present plus the adverb ending -ly; the base goes back to a Latin adjective for what is in front of someone, and the adverb splits between soon and now.
intro.cn: presently 是 present 加副词后缀 -ly；词干可追到表示「在某人面前」的拉丁形容词，副词义则在「不久」与「现在」之间分叉。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it placed the word at the near edge of a scene.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，把词义放在场景的近处边缘。

items.en: The verb esse meant to be or to exist, and its participle supplied the idea of something actually being there.
items.cn: 动词 esse 意为「存在、是」，其分词提供了「确实在那里」这一层意思。

items.en: Praesens described a person or thing that is here in front of the eyes, and it became the English adjective present.
items.cn: praesens 描述就在眼前的人或物，后来成为英语形容词 present。

items.en: Middle English joined present with the native adverb ending -ly, and the new word could already mean both at this time and after a little while.
items.cn: 中古英语把 present 与本地副词后缀 -ly 结合，新词当时已兼指「此时」与「过一会儿」。

items.en: British usage long favoured the sense soon, while American usage settled on at the present time, so the adverb now needs context to be read correctly.
items.cn: 英式用法长期偏向「不久」，美式用法则固定在「目前」，所以今天读到这个词要依靠上下文判断。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the present family built on Latin praesens; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of time close to now.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语 praesens 衍生出的 present 词族展开；近义组收表示「靠近此刻」的时间副词。

entries.definition: Being here now, or the current period.
entries.definitionCN: 现在的；在场的；当前时期。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在场；出席；存在。

entries.definition: A talk that shows and explains something.
entries.definitionCN: 展示并讲解某事的报告。

entries.definition: Belonging to the current period.
entries.definitionCN: 当今的；当前的。

entries.definition: After a short time from now.
entries.definitionCN: 从现在起很短时间之后；不久。

entries.definition: At the present time.
entries.definitionCN: 目前；当前。

entries.definition: In a little while, or briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 不久；简短地。

entries.definition: At this exact moment.
entries.definitionCN: 就在此刻；现在。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective present bent into an adverb; its family keeps circling the idea of being here, at this point in time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由形容词 present 折成副词；同族词始终围绕「就在这里、就在此刻」展开。

normal.en: Presently is present plus -ly, so the adverb keeps the idea of what is here at this moment.
normal.cn: presently 是 present 加 -ly，所以副词保留了「此刻就在这里」的意思。

normal.en: The same ending -ly appears in quickly and slowly, turning an adjective into a word about time or manner.
normal.cn: 同样的 -ly 也出现在 quickly 与 slowly 里，把形容词变成表示时间或方式的词。

normal.en: Presence and presently share praesens: one names being here, the other names the time around here.
normal.cn: presence 与 presently 共用 praesens：一个指「在这里」，另一个指「这附近的时间」。

normal.en: In British writing presently often means soon, while in American writing it usually means now, so the sentence, not the spelling, decides.
normal.cn: 英式写作里 presently 常指「不久」，美式写作里多指「现在」，所以决定词义的是句子而不是拼写。

normal.en: The phrase presently available is a safe test: it almost always means available now, not available soon.
normal.cn: presently available 是个稳妥的检验：它几乎总指「现在就可用的」，而不是「很快可用」。

abstract.en: A word that means both soon and now shows how thin the line is between the moment just ahead and the moment we already stand in.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示「不久」和「现在」，说明「即将到来」与「已经身处其中」之间只隔一条很细的线。

abstract.en: Presently is what happens when a word for being here is bent into a word for time.
abstract.cn: presently 就是一个表示「在这里」的词被折成表示时间的词之后的样子。

abstract.en: Reading presently correctly means asking where the speaker is standing: before the event, or inside it.
abstract.cn: 要读对 presently，就得问说话人站在哪里：事件之前，还是事件之中。

examples.en: The doctor will see you presently.
examples.cn: 医生很快就会给你看诊。

examples.en: The office is presently closed for repairs.
examples.cn: 办公室目前因维修关闭。

examples.en: All presently available seats are listed on the board.
examples.cn: 目前可用的座位都列在牌子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞怎特利」——先「在眼前」，再「马上来」；谐音只助记，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在场的）→ 英语 present + 副词后缀 -ly → presently；词干义为「此刻在眼前」，副词由此兼指「现在」与「不久」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is nearness in time; one branch leans forward to a moment shortly after now, the other stays on the current moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是时间上的「贴近」；一条分支向前指说话之后不久的时点，另一条停在当前这一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a station looking at a watch, saying the train comes in a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台上的人看着表，说列车一会儿就到。

branches.en: a sign reading closed for repairs
branches.cn: 写着维修期间暂停开放的告示

branches.en: a train announced a few minutes away
branches.cn: 广播说还有几分钟到站的列车

branches.en: a desk still holding today's papers
branches.cn: 桌上还摊着今天的文件

branches.en: a kettle just starting to whistle
branches.cn: 刚开始鸣叫的水壶

branches.en: a question left unanswered for now
branches.cn: 暂时没有答案的问题

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of presence plus an English adverb ending, and the family keeps the same two pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「在场」的拉丁形容词加英语副词后缀，整个词族都保留这两块构件。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: in the manner of, at the time of

definition_zh: 保存；保护；维持；果酱；自然保护区；专属领域
definition_en: to keep something in its original state, or to protect it from harm or change
core_image: 一排玻璃罐把夏天的果子封在糖水里，罐外的果园已经落光了叶子
scene: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐却把夏天的收成保存了下来。Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
sceneCN: 这里 preserve 指「用糖或盐把食物处理过，使其长期不坏」（第 5 个义项：以糖渍、腌渍等方式保存食物）；句意为果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。图中可辨识物件：玻璃罐、糖汁、果块、贴着手写日期的标签；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保存；保护；维持；腌制（食物）
蜜饯；果酱（常用复数）；自然保护区；专属领域

senses.title: Keep something from decaying
senses.definition: to treat or store something so that it does not decay
senses.definitionCN: 通过处理或存放使某物不腐坏
senses.example: Salt and smoke preserve meat through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 盐与烟熏能让肉在整个冬天不坏。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus servare 'keep' gives 'keep beforehand', and keeping food before it spoils is the oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: prae-「在前」加 servare「守住」得到「提前守住」，在食物变坏之前先护住，正是这个词最古老的用法。

senses.title: Protect a place from destruction
senses.titleCN: 保护地点、建筑不遭破坏或改造
senses.definition: to protect a building, place or object from being destroyed or altered
senses.definitionCN: 保护建筑、地点或物件不被摧毁或改动
senses.example: The trust preserves the medieval bridge exactly as it stands.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构让这座中世纪桥原样留存。
senses.why: the object sense keeps the core meaning untouched: what is preserved is not repaired into something new but kept as it was.
senses.whyCN: 物件义保持了核心含义：被 preserve 的不是被修成新东西，而是按原样留住。

senses.title: Keep a state or quality in being
senses.titleCN: 维持某种状态或品质继续存在
senses.definition: to keep a condition, quality or state continuing
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状况、品质或状态持续下去
senses.example: Officers preserved order while the crowd pushed forward.
senses.exampleCN: 人群向前涌时，警员维持着秩序。
senses.why: order is something that disappears unless it is actively kept, so the verb is used for conditions that need guarding.
senses.whyCN: 秩序若不主动守住就会消失，因此这个词也用于需要守护的状态。

senses.title: Keep something for later generations
senses.titleCN: 为后世留存记录或实物
senses.definition: to keep records, objects or knowledge so that people in the future can still use them
senses.definitionCN: 保存记录、实物或知识，使后人仍能使用
senses.example: Archivists preserve recordings of dialects that no longer have young speakers.
senses.exampleCN: 档案人员保存那些已无年轻使用者的方言录音。
senses.why: here the word looks forward: what is kept now is kept for a time the keeper will never see.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词朝向未来：此刻守住的东西，是为守者永远看不到的时代而留。

senses.title: Prepare fruit or meat with sugar or brine
senses.titleCN: 用糖渍、盐腌等方式加工食物
senses.definition: to prepare fruit or other food with sugar, salt or vinegar so that it keeps
senses.definitionCN: 用糖、盐或醋处理水果等食物以延长保存期
senses.example: Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
senses.exampleCN: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。
senses.why: the cooking sense specializes the general one: sugar and salt are the agents that do the guarding.
senses.whyCN: 烹调用法是一般义的具体化：糖与盐就是执行「守住」的媒介。

senses.title: A protected area of land
senses.definition: an area of land set aside so that its wildlife or landscape is protected
senses.definitionCN: 为保护野生生物或景观而划出的土地
senses.example: The marsh is a private preserve where hunting is banned.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽是私人保护区，禁止狩猎。
senses.why: the noun turns the act into a place: land where protection happens all the time.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把动作变成地点：持续进行保护的那片土地。

senses.title: Fruit jam in a jar
senses.titleCN: 果酱、蜜饯（美式常用复数）
senses.definition: fruit cooked with sugar and stored in jars
senses.definitionCN: 加糖熬煮后装罐的水果制品
senses.example: She opened a jar of strawberry preserves for the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她开了一罐草莓酱配吐司。
senses.why: the product noun is inherited straight from the verb, and American English prefers the plural for the jars on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 成品名词直接承自动词，美式英语更常用复数指架上的那些罐子。

senses.title: An activity reserved for one group
senses.titleCN: 某一群体独占的领域或活动
senses.definition: an activity or area that one group keeps for itself and others are shut out of
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体留给自己、他人不得进入的活动或领域
senses.example: Editing the paper is no longer a male preserve.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑这家报纸不再是男性的专属领域。
senses.why: the idea of keeping something safe for oneself shades easily into keeping others out, which is how this social sense arose.
senses.whyCN: 把某物为自己守住，很容易滑向把别人挡在外面，这个社会义就是这样产生的。

intro.en: Preserve comes through Old French from Latin praeservare, built on prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep'. It shares its root with conserve but not its prefix. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: preserve 经古法语来自拉丁 praeservare，由 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成。它与 conserve 共享词根，但前缀不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front of', and in compounds it often adds the idea of doing something in advance.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……之前」，在复合词中常添「预先」的意思。

items.en: Praeservare meant 'to keep or guard beforehand', a combination of the prefix with servare 'to keep safe'.
items.cn: praeservare 意为「提前看守、预先保住」，是前缀与 servare「守住」的组合。

items.en: Old French preserver brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, and the spelling settled as preserve.
items.cn: 古法语 preserver 在 14 世纪把词带入英语，拼写最终固定为 preserve。

items.en: The food sense is recorded from the sixteenth century; the sense of land set aside for wildlife developed in the nineteenth, when the first large reserves were mapped.
items.cn: 食物义在 16 世纪有记录；为野生生物划出土地的意思在 19 世纪形成，当时最早的几处大型保护区被勘定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for the jam noun and for the nature-reserve sense is not precisely recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of servare remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：果酱名词义与自然保护区义的最早书证没有确切记录；servare 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that share the Latin -serve stock and are easily mistaken; group two holds words that also mean keeping something safe but differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁 -serve 词干、容易认错的动词；第二组同样表示「保住」，但侧重点不同。

entries.definition: Com- plus servare stresses keeping a resource from being used up; preserve stresses keeping something from changing or spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 servare 强调不让资源被用尽；preserve 强调不让某物改变或变坏。

entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus servare: to set something aside instead of using it now, as in reserve a table.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 servare：把某物留到以后再用，如预订餐桌。

entries.definition: Ob- 'toward' plus servare: to watch, notice, or follow a rule; nothing is being stored.
entries.definitionCN: ob-「朝向」加 servare：观看、察觉或遵守规则；并不涉及储存。

entries.definition: De- 'fully' plus servire 'to serve': to have earned something. Same look, different root.
entries.definitionCN: de-「完全」加 servire「服侍」：因服务而应得。形似而词根不同。

entries.definition: To keep something safe from active harm; it says nothing about keeping it unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物免受主动伤害；不涉及保持原样。

entries.definition: To keep something one already has, such as heat or a right, without the idea of guarding it.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续保有已拥有之物，如热量或权利，不含守护之意。

entries.definition: To use a resource sparingly so that it lasts; its focus is quantity, not condition.
entries.definitionCN: 节制使用资源使其持久；关注的是数量而非状态。

entries.definition: To keep something working by servicing it, as a machine; preserve does not imply repair.
entries.definitionCN: 通过保养使某物继续运转，如机器；preserve 不含修理之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prae- 'before' + servare 'keep': guard it before harm arrives.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」+ servare「守住」：在伤害到来之前先护住。

normal.en: The family runs preserve, preservation, preservative, preserver, preservationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 preserve、preservation、preservative、preserver、preservationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: preserve food, preserve order, nature preserve, fruit preserves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：保存食物、维持秩序、自然保护区、果酱。

normal.en: The root is shared with conserve and reserve, but the prefixes do the dividing.
normal.cn: 词根与 conserve、reserve 共享，靠前缀区分。

normal.en: American English says preserves for jam, British English often says jam.
normal.cn: 美式英语用 preserves 指果酱，英式英语常用 jam。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of summer standing on a shelf in January.
abstract.cn: 想象一月的架子上摆着一罐夏天。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge left exactly as it was, weeds and all.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥连杂草都原样留着。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that keeps a meadow for animals and people out of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆把草场留给动物，把人挡在外面。

examples.en: The museum preserves the letters in acid-free boxes.
examples.cn: 博物馆把信件放在无酸盒中保存。

examples.en: Freezing preserves the flavour far better than drying.
examples.cn: 冷冻保存风味远胜于干燥。

examples.en: The old quarter is preserved as a living neighbourhood, not a museum.
examples.cn: 这片老城区是作为活着的社区被保护，而不是当成博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（提前）+ serve（守住）」——在坏掉之前先护住 → 保存、保护、维持

root: 拉丁 praeservare「提前守住」= prae-（在前）+ servare「看守、保存」；与 conserve 共享 servare 词根，靠前缀区分。英语 preserve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is guarded before harm reaches it, and that guard is then applied to food, buildings, order, records, land, jam and finally to a social boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：在损害到达之前先护住某物，这道防护再依次用于食物、建筑、秩序、记录、土地、果酱，最后用于一条社会边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jar and a fence, both keeping something whole against time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只罐与一道篱笆，都在对抗时间地把某物完整留住。

branches.en: STOP DECAY: sugar, salt and smoke are the guard, whether in a pot or a jar.
branches.cn: 止住腐坏：糖、盐与烟就是那道防护，无论在锅里还是罐里。

branches.en: UNCHANGED OBJECT: a building is kept as it stands, not restored into something new.
branches.cn: 原样的物件：建筑按现状留住，而不是修成新东西。

branches.en: STATE AND RECORD: order and archives both vanish unless someone keeps them.
branches.cn: 状态与记录：秩序与档案若无人守护都会消失。

branches.en: SET ASIDE: the act becomes a place, and the product becomes a jar.
branches.cn: 留出：动作变成一片地，成品变成一罐酱。

branches.en: KEPT FOR SOME: guarding something for oneself ends by shutting others out.
branches.cn: 为某些人留住：为自己守住，最终把别人挡在外面。

intro.en: Preserve is a Latin verb of prefix plus root; the same two parts build conserve, reserve and observe, so the family is best read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: preserve 是由前缀加词根构成的拉丁动词；同样的两部分也构成 conserve、reserve 与 observe，因此这个词族最好按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep' give praeservare; English draws preserve, preservation, preservative and preserver from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成 praeservare；英语由此得到 preserve、preservation、preservative 与 preserver。

items.example: The prefix marks action taken ahead of time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记提前采取的行动。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of guarding.
Salt preserves the fish before it spoils.
items.exampleCN: 盐在鱼变坏之前先把它保住。

items.example: Cold storage aids the preservation of vaccines.
items.exampleCN: 冷藏有助于疫苗的保存。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps food from spoiling
items.meaningCN: 防止食物变坏的添加物
items.exampleCN: 标签上未列出任何防腐剂。

items.meaning: a person or thing that preserves
items.example: He was a preserver of local songs.
items.exampleCN: 他是当地歌谣的保存者。

items.example: Dried grain is preservable for years.
items.exampleCN: 干燥的谷物可保存多年。

items.meaning: an advocate of protecting old buildings or land
items.meaningCN: 主张保护老建筑或土地的人
items.exampleCN: 保护主义者反对这次拆除。

items.example: They reserved two rooms for the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼留了两间房。

latinEntries.meaning: to keep beforehand, protect in advance

definition_zh: 总统；大学校长；董事长；会议主席
definition_en: the head of a state, a university, a company, or a meeting, especially one chosen to lead and to preside over others
core_image: 一张长桌的尽头，一个人坐在最前面的椅子上，所有人的目光都朝他那边
scene: 长桌两侧坐满了人，争论停不下来，最后大家都看向尽头那把椅子，等坐在那里的人开口。The president of the club called for a vote.
sceneCN: 这里 president 指「会长、会议主席」（第 4 个义项：被推举出来主持会议的人）；句意为俱乐部会长要求进行表决。图中可辨识物件：长桌、成排的椅子、举起的手。

collocations.phrase: the president of the United States

derivatives.zh: 由 president 换后缀 -cy 构成，义为「总统职位；任期」
由 president 加 -ial 构成，义为「总统的；总统制的」
与 president 同出拉丁 praesidere，义为「主持；担任主席」

senses.title: The head of a state
senses.definition: the elected head of a republic, who leads the government and represents the country
senses.definitionCN: 共和国的民选元首，领导政府并代表国家
senses.example: The president addressed the nation on television.
senses.exampleCN: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。
senses.why: The Latin source means to sit in front, and the leader of a state is pictured as the person seated at the head of the table where decisions are made.
senses.whyCN: 词源本义是「坐在前面」，国家领导人正被想象成长桌首位上坐着的人，所有决定都从他那里发出，因此「总统」是这个坐前意象在政治上的放大。

senses.title: The head of a university
senses.definition: the senior officer who leads a university or a college
senses.definitionCN: 领导一所大学或学院的最高负责人
senses.example: The president welcomed the new students at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在校门口迎接新生。
senses.why: A university is also a body with a council and a hall, so its leader inherits the same image of the person who sits before the assembly and speaks for it.
senses.whyCN: 大学同样有校务会议与礼堂，它的负责人也就继承了同一幅画面：坐在众人之前、代表整个机构讲话的人，于是这个词从国家元首平移到校长。

senses.title: The head of a company
senses.definition: the most senior officer of a company or organization
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构中职位最高的负责人
senses.example: The president of the firm signed the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司董事长签署了这份合同。
senses.why: Boards meet around a table, and the officer who sits at its head and signs for the company keeps the literal seating arrangement inside the modern title.
senses.whyCN: 董事会围桌而坐，坐在首位、代表公司签字的那个人，把「坐前排」的字面安排原样保留在现代头衔里，因此同一个词也指董事长、总裁。

senses.title: The person who chairs a meeting
senses.definition: the person chosen to lead a meeting, a club, or an assembly
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来主持聚会、俱乐部或集会的负责人
senses.example: The president of the club called for a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部会长要求进行表决。
senses.why: This is the plainest surviving sense: the one who sits in front of the group, keeps order, and lets others speak in turn.
senses.whyCN: 这是最贴近字面的一个义项：坐在一群人前面、维持秩序、安排轮流发言的人；规模没有国家或公司那么大，却仍是「坐前排」的原样动作。

intro.en: President goes back to a Latin verb made of a prefix meaning in front and a verb meaning to sit; the title first named anyone who sat before a group, then the head of a state.
intro.cn: president 可追到由「在前」的前缀与「坐」的动词组成的拉丁语动词；这个头衔最初指坐在一群人前面的人，后来才指国家元首。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it is the same element seen in many Latin words of rank and place.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，与许多表示位次和位置的拉丁词共用这一成分。

items.en: The verb sedere meant to sit, and it is the source of a wide family of English words about seats, sessions, and settling down.
items.cn: 动词 sedere 意为「坐」，派生出一大批关于座位、会议与安顿下来的英语词。

items.en: Praesidere joined the two: to sit before others, and therefore to watch over, guard, or lead an assembly.
items.cn: praesidere 把两者合起来：坐在别人前面，因此引申为看守、护卫、主持一个集会。

items.en: The present participle praesidens, with the stem praesident-, named the person who sits in front; this is the form English took.
items.cn: 现在分词 praesidens 的词干是 praesident-，指坐在前面的人，英语取用的正是这一形式。

items.en: Old French president passed the title into English, first for the officer of a meeting or a college, later for the head of a state and of a company.
items.cn: 古法语 president 把这个头衔传入英语，先指会议或学院的负责人，后来才指国家元首与公司最高负责人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for sitting in front; the near-meaning group gathers other titles for the person who leads a body.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「坐在前面」的拉丁动词展开；近义组收其他称呼团体领导者的头衔。

entries.definition: To be in charge of a meeting or ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 主持；担任会议或仪式的主席。

entries.definition: The office or the term of a president.
entries.definitionCN: 总统职位；任期。

entries.definition: Relating to a president or the office.
entries.definitionCN: 总统的；与总统职位有关的。

entries.definition: A standing committee that leads a larger body.
entries.definitionCN: 领导更大机构的常设委员会；主席团。

entries.definition: The person who leads a meeting or a committee.
entries.definitionCN: 主持会议或委员会的人；主席。

entries.definition: The head of a government, especially in some countries.
entries.definitionCN: 某些国家的政府首脑；总理。

entries.definition: The person in charge of a group or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 团体或机构的负责人。

entries.definition: The head of a school, especially in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指美国的学校校长。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin phrase turned into a title: the one who sits in front. Every sense keeps that seat at the head of the table.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个拉丁短语变成头衔：「坐在前面的人」；每个义项都保留着长桌首位那把椅子。

normal.en: President is prae- plus sedere: the one who sits in front of the others.
normal.cn: president 是 prae- 加 sedere：坐在其他人前面的那个人。

normal.en: Preside is the verb underneath the title, and presidency names the office or the term.
normal.cn: preside 是头衔底下的动词，presidency 则指职位或任期。

normal.en: Presidential adds -ial to make the adjective, as in a presidential election.
normal.cn: presidential 加 -ial 构成形容词，例如 a presidential election（总统选举）。

normal.en: The same Latin verb gave presidium, a standing committee that also sits in front of a larger body.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词也生出 presidium，指同样坐在更大机构前面的常设委员会。

normal.en: A club president and a company president share the title because both chair a body, not because both lead a country.
normal.cn: 俱乐部会长与公司董事长共用一个头衔，是因为两人都在主持一个团体，而不是因为两人都领导国家。

abstract.en: The oldest meaning is a seating plan: the person in the front chair gets to speak for everyone behind.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义其实是一张座次表：坐在前面椅子上的人，替后面所有人说话。

abstract.en: Power in this word is drawn as a place at the table, which is why the same title fits a state, a school, and a firm.
abstract.cn: 这个词里的权力被画成「桌边的一个位置」，所以同一个头衔能装下国家、学校与公司。

abstract.en: Whenever a group needs one voice, it looks for someone to sit at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 只要一个群体需要统一的声音，就会找一个人坐到长桌首位。

examples.en: The president addressed the nation on television.
examples.cn: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。

examples.en: The president of the university opened the ceremony.
examples.cn: 大学校长宣布典礼开始。

examples.en: She was elected president of the student union.
examples.cn: 她当选为学生会主席。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞兹登特」——坐在最前面的人（pre- 在前，sid 坐），就是主席与总统；谐音只助记。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ sedere（坐）→ praesidere（坐在前面、主持）→ 现在分词 praesidens（坐在前面的人）→ 古法语 president → 英语 president；字面就是「坐前排的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the seat at the front; the senses spread from chairing a small meeting to leading a university, a company, and a state.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「前排的座位」；义项从主持小会议，扩展到领导大学、公司与国家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table with one chair at its head and every face turned toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，尽头一把椅子，所有面孔都朝那边。

branches.en: a long table and one chair at its head
branches.cn: 一张长桌和尽头的一把椅子

branches.en: a hand raised to call for order
branches.cn: 举起要求安静的手

branches.en: a hall of freshmen waiting at the gate
branches.cn: 在校门口等候的新生

branches.en: a signature at the foot of a contract
branches.cn: 合同末尾的签名

branches.en: a broadcast from a desk to the whole country
branches.cn: 从办公桌后面传向全国的讲话

intro.en: The title is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb of sitting, its participle, and the English endings that name the office and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个头衔由拉丁前缀、表示「坐」的动词及其分词，再加上命名职位与性质的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

head of a meeting or body

latinEntries.meaning: to sit in front, to preside

definition_zh: 按；压；敦促；报刊；新闻界；出版社；榨取
definition_en: to push something firmly; to urge someone strongly; also newspapers and the people who produce them, a publishing house, or the act of squeezing juice or oil out
core_image: 一只手把按钮按到底，塑料外壳微微下陷，灯随即亮起
scene: 楼道里很暗，他伸出一根手指朝墙上的开关按下去，灯立刻亮起，脚步声也停了。Press the button twice if the door does not open.
sceneCN: 这里 press 指「按、压」（第 1 个义项：用手或工具对某物施加压力）；句意为如果门没开就按两次按钮。图中可辨识物件：墙上的开关、手指、走廊的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 press 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，义为「压力」
由 press 加 -ing 构成，义为「紧迫的；迫切的」
由 pressure 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「加压；密封加压」

senses.title: To push something firmly
senses.definition: to push steadily on something with the hand or a tool
senses.definitionCN: 用手或工具持续对某物施加推力
senses.example: Press the green button to start the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 按下绿色按钮启动机器。
senses.why: The Latin verb premere simply meant to press, and this physical push is the sense from which every other use of the word can be traced.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 premere 本义就是「压」，用手施加推力的这个动作是整个词义树的根，后面所有引申都能从这一下按压找到起点。

senses.title: To urge someone strongly
senses.definition: to try hard to persuade someone to do something, especially by repeating the request
senses.definitionCN: 反复请求以努力说服某人做某事
senses.example: The union pressed the government for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 工会敦促政府给出答复。
senses.why: Pressure applied to a person rather than an object becomes insistence, so the same verb moves from pushing a surface to pushing a decision forward.
senses.whyCN: 把压力从物体转到人身上，就变成了「不断施压、要求答复」，按压的动作没有变，只是受力的对象从按钮变成了决策者，因此产生「敦促」这一义。

senses.title: Newspapers and the people who make them
senses.definition: newspapers and magazines as a group, together with the journalists who work for them
senses.definitionCN: 报纸与杂志这一整体，以及为其工作的记者
senses.example: The story was widely reported in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事在新闻界被广泛报道。
senses.why: When printing presses made daily papers possible, the machine that pressed ink onto paper gave its name to the papers themselves and then to the whole profession.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机让日报成为可能，把油墨压到纸上的那台机器就用 press 来称呼，随后这个词从机器转到印出来的报纸，再扩指整个新闻行业。

senses.title: A publishing house
senses.definition: a company that prints and publishes books, or the business of publishing
senses.definitionCN: 印刷并出版书籍的公司，或出版这一行业
senses.example: The book came out under a small university press.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书由一家小型大学出版社出版。
senses.why: The same machine also names the firm that owns it, so press shifts from the equipment to the business that turns manuscripts into bound books.
senses.whyCN: 同一台机器也能代指拥有它的机构，于是 press 从设备滑向企业，用来指把书稿变成成书的出版社，这一义项至今保留在大学社名与出版品牌里。

senses.title: To squeeze out liquid
senses.definition: to squeeze fruit, seeds, or oil to get the liquid inside
senses.definitionCN: 挤压果实、种子或油料以取得其中的液体
senses.example: They press the olives within a day of picking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在采摘当天就把橄榄榨成油。
senses.why: Squeezing olives is the most literal kind of pressing, force applied until something flows out, and it survives beside the abstract senses.
senses.whyCN: 榨橄榄是最字面的一种「压」：一直加力，直到有东西流出来；这个用法与引申义长期并存，说明表示压力的词始终保留着「压出液体」的具体一面。

intro.en: Press comes from a Latin verb for pressing; a repeated-action form of it reached French and then English, and the printing machine later pushed the word into newspapers and publishing.
intro.cn: press 来自表示「压」的拉丁动词；它的反复体形式经法语进入英语，后来印刷机又把这个词推进报刊与出版领域。

items.en: The verb premere meant to press, squeeze, or push down, and it is the base of a large family of English words.
items.cn: 动词 premere 意为压、挤、向下推，是一大批英语词的共同基础。

items.en: A frequentative form pressare described pressing again and again, and this is the branch that travelled into French.
items.cn: pressare 是反复体形式，表示「一再压」，进入法语的正是这一支。

items.en: Old French presser kept both the physical sense and the sense of urging someone, and English borrowed it as pressen.
items.cn: 古法语 presser 同时保留「压」的具体义与「催促某人」的引申义，英语借入后写作 pressen。

items.en: Middle English press covered pushing, crowding, and the machine that pressed ink onto paper.
items.cn: 中古英语的 press 覆盖推、挤，以及把油墨压到纸上的机器。

items.en: Modern English lets the noun name the machine, the newspapers it produces, the publishing house, and the journalists as a body.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个名词同时指机器、机器印出的报纸、出版社，以及作为群体的新闻工作者。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for pressing and its English compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of force and words for the news industry.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「压」的拉丁词根及其英语复合词展开；近义组收施加力量的动词与新闻行业的说法。

entries.definition: A steady force acting on a surface, or strong influence on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 持续作用在表面上的力；对人所施的压力。

entries.definition: Needing attention right away.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立刻处理的；紧迫的。

entries.definition: To press things together into a smaller space.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西压到一起，使其占更小空间。

entries.definition: To put a thought into words, or to send something fast.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法说出来；快速送出。

entries.definition: To move something away by force.
entries.definitionCN: 用力把某物推开。

entries.definition: To press something from both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 从两侧挤压某物。

entries.definition: Newspapers, television, and other channels of news.
entries.definitionCN: 报纸、电视等新闻传播渠道。

entries.definition: To ask strongly that something be done.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈要求做某事。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing plus its repeated form; the family spreads from physical force to urging people and to printing words on paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「压」的拉丁动词及其反复体；词族从物理的力，扩展到催促人，再扩展到把字印到纸上。

normal.en: Press comes from Latin premere, to press, and its frequentative pressare gave the French verb that English borrowed.
normal.cn: press 来自拉丁语 premere（压），它的反复体 pressare 生出法语动词，再传入英语。

normal.en: Pressure is press plus -ure, the result of pressing: a force that keeps acting on a surface.
normal.cn: pressure 是 press 加 -ure，指压出来的结果：持续作用在表面上的力。

normal.en: Compress and express both keep the Latin root premere, one pressing things together, the other pressing ideas out.
normal.cn: compress 与 express 都保留拉丁词根 premere：一个把东西压到一起，一个把想法压出来。

normal.en: The printing press pressed ink into paper, and from that machine came the sense newspapers and journalists.
normal.cn: 印刷机把油墨压进纸里，而「报刊、记者」这一义正是从那台机器来的。

normal.en: Pressing as an adjective keeps the physical weight: a pressing problem is one that bears down on you now.
normal.cn: 形容词 pressing 保留了物理上的重量：a pressing problem 就是此刻压在你身上的问题。

abstract.en: Press is what force looks like when it has a direction: down on a button, out through an olive, or straight at a person who must answer.
abstract.cn: press 就是力有了方向之后的样子：向下按按钮，向外榨橄榄，或直直压向一个必须答复的人。

abstract.en: One machine that pushed ink into paper was enough to rename an entire profession.
abstract.cn: 一台把油墨压进纸里的机器，就足以给整个行业改名。

abstract.en: The word shows that persuasion and printing are both forms of applied pressure, one on people and one on surfaces.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明说服与印刷都是「加压力」的形式：一个作用在人身上，一个作用在表面上。

examples.en: Press the green button to start the machine.
examples.cn: 按下绿色按钮启动机器。

examples.en: The story was widely reported in the press.
examples.cn: 这件事在新闻界被广泛报道。

examples.en: She pressed the olives by hand.
examples.cn: 她用手把橄榄榨成油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷斯」——手掌往下一「压」，就是 press；压出来的报纸也叫 press。谐音只助记。

root: 拉丁语 premere（压）→ 反复体 pressare（一再压）→ 古法语 presser → 中古英语 pressen → 英语 press；从「按压」引申出「施压敦促」，再由印刷机引申出「报刊、新闻界、出版社」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is downward force; the senses divide into physical pressing, pressure on people, squeezing out liquid, and the printing machine with everything it produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是向下的力；义项由此分为物理按压、对人施压、榨出液体，以及印刷机及其产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger driving a button to its stop until the lamp answers with light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指把按钮按到底，灯以亮起作为回应。

branches.cn: 手指把按钮按到底

branches.en: olive oil running into a jar
branches.cn: 橄榄油流进罐子

branches.en: a repeated request left on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上反复递上的请求

branches.en: a folded newspaper on a breakfast table
branches.cn: 早餐桌上折起的报纸

branches.cn: 书末页上的出版标记

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its repeated form, the French verb taken from it, and the English endings that name the force and the action.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「压」的拉丁动词、其反复体、由它而来的法语动词，以及命名压力与动作的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

items.meaning: a steady force on a surface
a machine that prints on paper

definition_zh: 压力；压强；血压；心理压力；催逼；紧迫的负担
definition_en: the force pressing on a surface per unit area; also the feeling of strain, or the act of urging someone to do something
core_image: 一只手掌按在桌面上，桌板把整份重量分散到整个接触面
scene: 潜水员下潜到十米深处，耳膜被水压压得发紧，呼吸也变得费力。The pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
sceneCN: 这里 pressure 指「单位面积上所受的力」（第 1 个义项：压力、压强）；句意为每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。图中可辨识物件：潜水员、面罩、深度绳、气泡；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 心理压力；催逼；紧迫的负担

senses.title: Force per unit area
senses.definition: the force acting on a surface divided by the area of that surface
senses.definitionCN: 作用在表面上的力除以该表面的面积
senses.example: Pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
senses.exampleCN: 每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。
senses.why: Latin pressura named a pressing, and physics gave the word a precise ratio of force to area.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 pressura 本指「压」，物理学给了这个词「力与面积之比」的精确含义。

senses.title: Pressure in a gas or liquid
senses.definition: the internal pressure of a fluid, measured in pascals or bar
senses.definitionCN: 流体的内部压强，以帕或巴计
senses.example: The gas pressure in the cylinder doubled when it was heated.
senses.exampleCN: 钢瓶受热时，瓶内气体压强翻倍。
senses.why: fluids push outward in all directions, and the word measures that push.
senses.whyCN: 流体会向各个方向推，这个词测的就是这种推力。

senses.title: Blood pressure
senses.definition: the force with which blood presses against the walls of the arteries
senses.definitionCN: 血液对动脉壁施加的力
senses.example: His blood pressure rose during the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 他在攀登过程中血压升高。
senses.why: medicine applied the physical word to the body's own plumbing.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个物理词用到人体自身的管道上。

senses.title: Psychological strain
senses.definition: the mental strain produced by demands that seem to exceed one's capacity
senses.definitionCN: 由似乎超出承受能力的要求造成的心理紧张
senses.example: The pressure of the final week kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一周的压力让她睡不着。
senses.why: something weighing on the mind behaves like a weight on a surface, so the physical word serves feeling too.
senses.whyCN: 压在心头的东西行为像压在表面上的重量，于是物理词也服务感受。

senses.title: Social pressure
senses.definition: the influence of a group that pushes a person toward a particular choice
senses.definitionCN: 群体推动个人做出某种选择的影响
senses.example: Peer pressure made the younger students hide their doubts.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴压力让年纪较小的学生藏起自己的疑虑。
senses.why: a group can press on a person as steadily as a hand on a table.
senses.whyCN: 群体能像按在桌上的手一样，稳稳地压住一个人。

senses.title: The act of urging
senses.definition: the act of repeatedly urging or persuading someone to act
senses.definitionCN: 反复催促或说服某人采取行动的行为
senses.example: The committee applied pressure until the report was released.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不断施压，直到报告被公布。
senses.why: pressing someone is the literal action of the Latin verb, carried into social life.
senses.whyCN: 催促某人正是那个拉丁动词的字面动作进入社会生活。

senses.title: The burden of demands
senses.titleCN: 工作与时间的紧迫负担
senses.definition: the weight of urgent work, deadlines or expectations
senses.definitionCN: 紧急工作、截止期限或期待带来的重负
senses.example: The staff worked under constant pressure during the season.
senses.exampleCN: 旺季期间员工一直在压力下工作。
senses.why: time and tasks can also pile up like a physical load.
senses.whyCN: 时间与任务也会像实物一样堆积起来。

senses.title: A weather system
senses.definition: a region of high or low atmospheric pressure shown on a weather map
senses.definitionCN: 天气图上标出的高压或低压区域
senses.example: A deep low pressure system crossed the coast overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一个深厚的低压系统一夜之间越过海岸。
senses.why: meteorology uses pressure as the variable that organises the whole map.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把气压当作组织整张天气图的变量。

intro.en: Pressure comes through Old French from Latin pressura 'a pressing', a noun from premere 'to press, squeeze'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pressure 经古法语来自拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」，它是 premere「压、挤」的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze, hold down'; its past participle pressus lies behind the noun and the English verb press.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤、按住」，其过去分词 pressus 是名词与英语动词 press 的来源。

items.en: Pressura 'a pressing, pressure' was formed from the participle and used for the act and its result.
items.cn: pressura「压、挤压」由分词构成，既指动作也指结果。

items.en: Old French pressure and Latin pressura gave English pressure in the late fourteenth century, first meaning anguish or the act of pressing.
items.cn: 古法语 pressure 与拉丁 pressura 在十四世纪末给出英语 pressure，最初指痛苦或按压的动作。

items.en: The force-per-area sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when experiments on air and fluids needed a precise term.
items.cn: 单位面积受力的物理义从十七世纪有记录，当时对空气与流体的实验需要一个精确术语。

items.en: Blood pressure appears in the eighteenth century, while the figurative senses of urgency and coercion grow from the same idea of something weighing down.
items.cn: 血压的用法出现在十八世纪，而紧迫与催逼的比喻义都从「有东西压下来」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: First English dates approximate: the earliest English use is usually dated to the late fourteenth century and the first physics citation to the seventeenth, though neither date is exact.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：英语最早用法通常定在十四世纪末，最早的物理书证定在十七世纪，但两者都不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same verb that are not the noun; group two holds nouns for force, strain and tension.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词来的形式、却不是这个名词；第二组是表示力、紧张与张力的名词。

entries.definition: The verb means to push down; as a noun it means the printing machines or the news media, not force per area.
entries.definitionCN: 动词意为向下按；作名词指印刷机或新闻界，而非单位面积上的力。

entries.definition: To keep the air in a cabin or tank at a chosen pressure; it acts on a space, not on a person's mind.
entries.definitionCN: 让机舱或容器中的空气保持某一压强；作用于空间，不作用于人的心理。

entries.definition: As an adjective it means urgent; as a noun it means an act of ironing or a batch of records.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为紧迫的；作名词指熨烫动作或一批唱片。

entries.definition: Describing someone who is subjected to pressure; it is not the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容承受压力的人；并非名词本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for strain on a person or material; pressure is the force, stress is often the response.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或材料所受紧张的更宽泛词；pressure 偏力，stress 常指反应。

entries.definition: The deformation or damage caused by a load; it describes the effect rather than the pushing force.
entries.definitionCN: 载荷造成的变形或损伤；描述结果，而非推力。

entries.definition: A pulling force along a rope or a nervous stretch; the opposite direction from pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 沿绳的拉力或神经上的紧绷；方向与压力相反。

entries.definition: A push or pull without reference to area; pressure is force divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 不涉及面积的推或拉；pressure 是力除以面积。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin premere 'press' gives press, pressure, pressurize, pressing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 premere「压」给出 press、pressure、pressurize、pressing。

normal.en: Physics defines it as force divided by area; the unit is the pascal.
normal.cn: 物理学把它定义力除以面积，单位是帕。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: under pressure, blood pressure, high pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：在压力之下、血压、高压。

normal.en: The same word serves a diver's mask, a hospital ward and a committee room.
normal.cn: 同一个词服务潜水员的面罩、医院病房与委员会会议室。

normal.en: A weather map is drawn in pressure, with highs and lows.
normal.cn: 天气图以气压绘制，标出高压与低压。

abstract.en: Picture a palm flat on a table, the weight spread across the whole contact.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌平放在桌上，重量摊在整个接触面。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaning toward one person until that person moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人向一个人倾压过去，直到那人让步。

abstract.en: Picture a column of water above a small mask, growing heavier metre by metre.
abstract.cn: 想象一小块面罩上方的水柱，一米一米地变重。

examples.en: The pressure inside the tank was too high for the valve.
examples.cn: 罐内压力对阀门来说过高。

examples.en: She felt the pressure of the deadline all week.
examples.cn: 她整个星期都感到截止期的压力。

examples.en: A low pressure system brought rain to the coast.
examples.cn: 一个低压系统给沿海带来降雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: press 是「压」，-ure 是名词后缀：压下去的那个力量 → 压力；物理上是单位面积上的力，心上就是心理压力

root: 拉丁 premere「压、挤」→ pressus → pressura「压」→ 古法语 pressure → 英语 pressure；引申为血压、心理压力与气压。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressing force: the physical quantity, the pressure inside a fluid, blood pressure, mental strain, group pressure, the act of urging, the burden of urgent work and finally a weather system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种压下的力展开：物理量、流体内压、血压、心理紧张、群体压力、催逼的动作、紧迫工作的重负，最后是一个天气系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat palm on a table, its weight spread over the whole contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只平放的手掌，重量摊在整个接触面上。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL RATIO: force over area, and the same push inside a fluid.
branches.cn: 物理比值：力除以面积，以及流体内部的同一种推。

branches.en: THE BODY'S PLUMBING: blood presses on artery walls.
branches.cn: 人体的管道：血液压住动脉壁。

branches.en: THE INNER LOAD: strain and the pile of urgent demands both weigh on a person.
branches.cn: 内在负荷：紧张与堆积的紧急要求都压在人身上。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL PUSH: a group can press, and so can a committee.
branches.cn: 社会推力：群体能施压，委员会也能。

branches.en: THE WEATHER MAP: pressure becomes the variable that organises highs and lows.
branches.cn: 天气图：气压成为组织高低压的变量。

intro.en: Pressure is a Latin noun built on a verb, and that verb also gives the everyday English word press.
intro.cn: pressure 是建立在动词上的拉丁名词，那个动词也给出日常英语词 press。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere 'to press' and pressura 'a pressing' stand behind pressure, press, pressurize and pressing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 premere「压」与 pressura「压、挤压」是 pressure、press、pressurize 与 pressing 的来源。

items.example: The verb is the physical act behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是每个义项背后的物理动作。

items.example: The noun names the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指动作及其结果。

items.meaning: to push down; the news media
to keep a space at a chosen pressure
items.example: The cabin is pressurized for flight.

items.meaning: kept at higher than ambient pressure
items.example: A pressurized tank stores the gas.

items.meaning: the act of keeping a pressure

items.example: A pressing matter needed an answer.
items.exampleCN: 一件紧迫的事需要答复。

definition_zh: 据推测；大概；想必
definition_en: as may reasonably be supposed from the available evidence
core_image: 桌上的伞还在滴水，主人却不在，读者据此猜他刚回来
scene: 实验室的门锁着，灯却亮着，同事据此推断有人来过。The lights are on, so someone is presumably still inside.
sceneCN: 这里指根据迹象作出的合理推测（第 1 个义项：据推测）；句意为灯还亮着，所以想必里面还有人；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: As one may reasonably suppose
senses.definition: used to state what may reasonably be believed from the available evidence
senses.definitionCN: 说明根据现有证据可以合理相信的内容
senses.example: Presumably, the train was delayed by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 据推测，火车是被暴风雨耽误了。
senses.why: The adverb presents an inference, not a fact: the speaker expects the listener to accept the reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词呈现的是推断而非事实：说话者期待听者接受这套推理。

senses.title: Probably, but unconfirmed
senses.definition: used of a likely fact that has not been checked
senses.definitionCN: 指很可能成立却尚未核实的事实
senses.example: The keys are presumably in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙想必在抽屉里。
senses.why: The word marks probability resting on a normal expectation rather than on proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的是建立在通常预期上的可能性，而不是证据。

senses.title: Sentence-opening inference
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, presenting a conclusion drawn from what precedes
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，呈现由前文推出的结论
senses.example: Presumably, the author meant a different example.
senses.exampleCN: 想必作者想说的是另一个例子。
senses.why: The initial position frames the whole clause as a reader's inference, common in commentary.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把整个小句框成读者的推断，这在评注文字中很常见。

senses.title: Presumably because
senses.definition: used to offer a likely explanation for something
senses.definitionCN: 用来为某事提出一个很可能的解释
senses.example: Presumably because of the rain, the match was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 想必是因为下雨，比赛被取消了。
senses.why: The pattern assigns a probable cause without claiming direct knowledge of it.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式给出可能的成因，却不声称直接知道它。

senses.title: Presumably not
senses.definition: used with not to state a likely negative conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，说出一个很可能的否定结论
senses.example: Presumably not everyone agreed with the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 想必并非人人都同意这个决定。
senses.why: Negation keeps the hedging: the speaker infers a negative rather than asserting it.
senses.whyCN: 否定保留了缓冲：说话者是在推断一个否定，而不是断言。

senses.title: Hedging in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的推测语气
senses.definition: in scholarship, a courteous way to attribute an unstated intention to an author
senses.definitionCN: 在学术写作中，礼貌地把未明说的意图归给作者
senses.example: The passage is presumably an allusion to an older text.
senses.exampleCN: 这段文字想必是在暗指一部更早的文本。
senses.why: The hedge protects the writer from overclaiming about another person's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这一缓冲保护作者，免得对他人的意思说得过满。

senses.title: Legal presumption
senses.definition: in law, describing a fact treated as true unless it is rebutted
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，指除非被反驳否则视为真实的事实
senses.example: A person is presumably innocent until the case is proved.
senses.exampleCN: 在案件被证实之前，一个人被推定无罪。
senses.why: Legal usage turns the adverb into a rule about the burden of proof, not a casual guess.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个副词变成关于举证责任的规则，而不是随口猜测。

senses.title: Ironic dismissal
senses.definition: in speech, used ironically to suggest that something is only supposedly true
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中反讽地表示某事只是「据说」成立
senses.example: Presumably, that explanation satisfies everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 想必这个解释能让所有人满意吧。
senses.why: The ironic tone leans on the word's hedging: the speaker repeats a claim while doubting it.
senses.whyCN: 反讽语气借用了这个词的缓冲：说话者重复一个说法，同时表示怀疑。

intro.en: Presumably comes from the Latin verb for taking beforehand, through its noun and English adjective, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「预先拿取」的动词，经名词与英语形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb sumere means to take or take up.
items.cn: 动词意为「拿、取」。

items.en: The prefix prae- means before or in advance.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前、预先」。

items.en: Praesumere means to take in advance, hence to assume or anticipate.
items.cn: 合成动词意为「预先拿走」，引申为「假定、预料」。

items.en: The noun praesumptio names an assumption taken beforehand.
items.cn: 名词指事先采取的假定。

items.en: English presume and presumable come through French and law; the adverb adds the usual suffix.
items.cn: 英语经法语与法学传统借入「假定」及其形容词，副词再加常见后缀。

items.en: Modern prose uses the adverb as a polite hedge in inference and academic commentary; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 现代散文用它作推断与学术评论中的礼貌缓冲；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin take-beforehand family, including a word with a stronger negative sense; the second group contrasts inference from evidence with plain probability.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「预先拿取」词族，其中包括一个贬义更强的词；第二组对照「由证据推断」与「单纯的可能性」。

entries.definition: To suppose something to be true before proof; also to dare without permission.
entries.definitionCN: 在证据前就假定为真；也指未经许可擅自。

entries.definition: An assumption taken as true, or behaviour that goes too far.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为真的假定，或越界的行为。

entries.definition: Able to be supposed; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 可以推定的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: Going beyond what one has the right to do; the negative branch of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 越出本分、冒昧的；词族的贬义分支。

entries.definition: In all likelihood, without necessarily resting on a stated chain of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能，但不一定建立在明说的证据链上。

entries.definition: A formal phrase meaning very probably.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「很可能」的正式短语。

entries.definition: According to the normal course of things.
entries.definitionCN: 按照事情的通常走向。

entries.definition: Certainly or very probably; a stronger and older word.
entries.definitionCN: 确实或很可能；更强、更旧的词。

entries.definition: As it appears from what is seen or reported, without proof.
entries.definitionCN: 从所见或所闻看来如此，但未经证实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real take-beforehand root and the real difference between inference and plain probability.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「预先拿取」词根，并区分「推断」与「单纯可能」。

normal.en: The root means to take beforehand, so the speaker takes a conclusion before the proof arrives.
normal.cn: 词根意为「预先拿取」，所以说话者在证据到之前先把结论拿来。

normal.en: The lights are on, so someone is presumably inside: evidence first, conclusion second.
normal.cn: 灯亮着，所以想必有人在里面：先有迹象，再有结论。

normal.en: Presumably because does the same work as probably because, but sounds more careful.
normal.cn: 「想必是因为」与「很可能是因为」作用相同，但听起来更谨慎。

normal.en: In academic prose it lets a writer guess at an author's intention without claiming to know it.
normal.cn: 在学术文字里，它让作者猜测原作者意图，却不声称知道。

normal.en: In law, presumably innocent is a rule about who must prove what.
normal.cn: 在法律里，「推定无罪」是一条关于谁来举证的规定。

abstract.en: To presume is to lend a fact before it has earned trust.
abstract.cn: 推测就是在一件事尚未赢得信任之前先借给它。

abstract.en: The hedge keeps the door open in case the inference turns out wrong.
abstract.cn: 缓冲把门留着，以防推断最后错了。

abstract.en: Irony here works by repeating a claim with the doubt left showing at the edges.
abstract.cn: 这里的反讽靠重复一个说法，却让怀疑留在边缘。

examples.en: Presumably, the meeting was moved because of the holiday.
examples.cn: 想必会议是因为假日而改期。

examples.en: The document is presumably a copy, not the original.
examples.cn: 这份文件想必是副本，而不是原件。

examples.en: Presumably not all the guests were invited.
examples.cn: 想必并非所有客人都受到了邀请。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普瑞祖母布里」——祖母凭经验猜，大概如此

root: 拉丁语动词「拿取」加表示「预先」的前缀，构成「预先拿走、假定」，其名词指事先采取的假定；英语经法语与法学传统借入动词与形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate evidence-based inference, unconfirmed probability, sentence-opening inference, likely explanation, negated inference, academic hedging, legal presumption and ironic doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理据证推断、未证实的可能、句首推断、可能解释、否定推断、学术缓冲、法律推定，以及反讽怀疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping umbrella on the table while its owner is missing, so the reader guesses he just came in.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的伞还在滴水，主人却不在，读者据此猜他刚进来。

branches.en: THE INFERENCE: evidence leads to a conclusion, whether inside the sentence or at its head.
branches.cn: 推断：证据引出结论，无论在句中还是句首。

branches.en: THE UNCHECKED FACT: likely by normal expectation, not proved.
branches.cn: 未核事实：按通常预期很可能，却未获证明。

branches.en: THE LIKELY CAUSE: a probable explanation offered without direct knowledge.
branches.cn: 可能成因：在没有直接知识时给出的合理解释。

branches.en: THE HEDGE: negated inference and the courteous academic buffer.
branches.cn: 缓冲：否定式推断与学术上的礼貌缓冲。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE IRONY: legal burden of proof and the sceptical repeat.
branches.cn: 规则与反讽：法律举证责任与带怀疑的重复。

intro.en: Presumably is a Latin before-prefix, a taking-root, a noun of assumption, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「预先」前缀、「拿取」词根、表「假定」的名词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root is taking; the prefix puts the taking before the fact, which is exactly what an assumption does.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是「拿取」；前缀把拿取放在事实之前，这正是「假定」所做的事。

items.example: The prefix puts the action ahead of the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放在证据之前。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical act of taking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「拿取」的具体动作。

items.example: The compound verb turns taking early into assuming.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词把「提前拿」变成「假定」。

items.example: The suffix builds the noun of assumption.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表「假定」的名词。

items.example: The noun is the base of the English legal term.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语法律术语的基词。

items.example: English keeps both the thinking and the daring senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留「思考」与「大胆」两条义。

items.example: The noun carries the same double life.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词也带着同样的双重身份。

items.example: A different suffix pulls out the negative branch.
items.exampleCN: 另一个后缀拉出贬义分支。

items.example: The suffix turns presumable into a hedge adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成缓冲副词。

definition_zh: 假定；推测；擅自；胆敢；（法律）推定
definition_en: to suppose something is true without proof, or to dare to do something without permission
core_image: 还没进门就先假定门里的灯是亮的，抬脚就走
scene: 电话一直没人接。Because no one answered the phone, she could only presume that her friend was already on the way, so she went straight to the station to wait.
sceneCN: 这里 presume 是「假定、推测」（第 1 个义项：在没有证据时先认定某事为真）；句意：因为没人接电话，她只能假定朋友已经在路上，于是直接去车站等。图中可辨识物件：无人接听的电话、时刻表、车站长椅、行李箱、手表；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe something is true before there is proof
senses.definitionCN: 在证据之前就相信某事为真
senses.example: I presume you have read the report.
senses.exampleCN: 我想你已经读过报告了。
senses.why: Latin praesumere means 'take before': prae- 'before' plus sumere 'take'. The mind takes a proposition as a starting point rather than waiting for evidence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praesumere 意为“先取”：prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”。心智把某个命题先拿来做起点，而不等证据。

senses.title: Take for granted
senses.definition: to accept something as true without checking it
senses.definitionCN: 不加核对就接受某事为真
senses.example: We presume the train will be on time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们想当然地认为火车会准点。
senses.why: The everyday sense is a habit of the mind: what is normally true is taken as true again. Presumption is assumption made comfortable by repetition.
senses.whyCN: 日常义是一种心智习惯：通常为真的事，就再当作真。推定是被重复养得舒服的假定。

senses.title: Assume legally (presumed innocent)
senses.definition: in law, to treat a fact as established until disproved
senses.definitionCN: 法律中，在未被反驳前把某事实视为成立
senses.example: A defendant is presumed innocent until proved guilty.
senses.exampleCN: 被告在被证明有罪前被推定无罪。
senses.why: Legal systems must act before certainty. Presumption supplies a default that can be attacked by evidence, so the burden of proof is allocated by the word.
senses.whyCN: 法律系统必须在确定之前行动。推定提供一个可被证据攻击的默认值，于是证明责任由这个词来分配。

senses.title: Dare to do something
senses.definition: to venture to do something that may be unwelcome or beyond your right
senses.definitionCN: 贸然做可能不受欢迎或越权的事
senses.example: I would not presume to tell you your job.
senses.exampleCN: 我不敢冒昧指点你的工作。
senses.why: The 'take before' image turns social: to presume is to take a step before permission is given. The act is not illegal, only ahead of its warrant.
senses.whyCN: “先取”意象转向社会：presume 是在许可之前先迈一步。这行为不违法，只是走在了授权之前。

senses.title: Be presumptuous or overbold
senses.definition: to behave with more confidence or freedom than is proper
senses.definitionCN: 以超出分寸的自信或自由行事
senses.example: He presumed too far with his host's kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 他过于利用主人的好意了。
senses.why: When the object is another person's goodwill, 'taking before' becomes taking advantage. The adjective presumptuous names this excess directly.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是他人的善意，“先取”就变成占便宜。形容词 presumptuous 直接命名这种越界。

senses.title: Take advantage of (presume on)
senses.definition: to rely too much on someone's tolerance or generosity
senses.definitionCN: 过度依赖某人的宽容或慷慨
senses.example: She presumed on their hospitality and stayed a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她仗着他们的好客住了一个月。
senses.why: The phrasal verb marks the target of the taking: what is presumed upon is the patience of another. The word records a debt that was never asked for.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语动词标出“取”的对象：被 presume upon 的是他人的耐心。这个词记录了一笔从未被同意的亏欠。

senses.title: Suppose as a working hypothesis
senses.definition: to adopt a proposition provisionally in order to reason from it
senses.definitionCN: 为推理而暂时采用一个命题
senses.example: Presume the data are accurate and see what follows.
senses.exampleCN: 假定数据准确，看看会推出什么。
senses.why: In logic and science a presumption is a deliberate starting point. The word asks the listener to grant it for the sake of the argument, not to believe it outright.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑与科学中，presumption 是刻意的起点。这个词请听者为了论证暂时承认它，而不是彻底相信它。

senses.title: Presume death after absence
senses.definition: in law, to declare a missing person dead after a set period
senses.definitionCN: 法律中，在特定期限后宣告失踪者死亡
senses.example: The court presumed him dead after seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 七年后法庭推定他已死亡。
senses.why: This is presumption at its most literal: the law cannot see the person, so it takes the most probable fact and acts on it. The missing body is replaced by a legal certainty.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的推定：法律看不见那个人，于是取最可能的事实并据此行动。失踪的身体被一个法律确定性取代。

senses.title: Believe on probability
senses.definition: to hold a belief because it is likely, not because it is proved
senses.definitionCN: 因某事很可能而相信，而非因已证明
senses.example: We presume the cause was a short circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们推测原因是短路。
senses.why: The word's epistemic core: belief proportioned to likelihood. It sits between guess (weak) and know (strong), and usually signals that the speaker is aware of the gap.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的认识论核心：与可能性相称的相信。它位于 guess（弱）与 know（强）之间，通常表示说话者意识到那道缺口。

intro.en: Presume is built from 'take before': prae- 'before' plus sumere 'to take'. It differs from assume, which is 'take to oneself'. The legal and social senses grow from that single gesture of taking ahead of proof or permission.
intro.cn: presume 由“先取”构成：prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”。它与 assume（“取到自己身上”）不同。法律义与社会义都从这一个“在证据或许可之前先取”的动作生长出来。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'take upon oneself, venture, dare'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“承担、冒险、胆敢”之义。

items.en: From Latin praesumere 'take before, take for granted, anticipate' = prae- 'before' + sumere 'take up'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 praesumere“先取、视为当然、预料”= prae-“在前”+ sumere“取起”。

items.en: sumere is sub- 'under' + emere 'take, buy', the verb behind assume, consume, resume, and sumption. Presume takes before; assume takes to oneself.
items.cn: sumere 是 sub-“在下”+ emere“取、买”，也是 assume、consume、resume、sumption 的动词。presume 是先取，assume 是取到自己身上。

items.en: The legal sense 'take as established until disproved' develops, giving presumption and presumptive.
items.cn: 法律义“在未被反驳前视为成立”发展出来，产生 presumption 与 presumptive。

items.en: The negative social sense 'overbold, taking too much upon oneself' produces presumptuous.
items.cn: 负面的社会义“过分大胆、越权”产生 presumptuous。

items.en: Modern English keeps both faces: an epistemic default and a social trespass. Presumably marks the first; presumptuous marks the second.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两副面孔：认识上的默认与社会上的越界。presumably 标记前者，presumptuous 标记后者。

note.en: The first group shares the sumere root and the -sume spelling; the second is about verbs that also mean supposing or daring.
note.cn: 第一组共享 sumere 词根与 -sume 拼写，第二组看同样表示“假定”或“胆敢”的动词。

entries.definition: to take as true, or to take power. It uses ad- 'to' + sumere, taking to oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 假定；承担；夺取。它用 ad-“向”+ sumere，取到自己身上。

entries.definition: to begin again after a pause. It is re- 'again' + sumere.
entries.definitionCN: 暂停后再开始。它是 re-“再”+ sumere。

entries.definition: a belief taken for granted, or boldness. It is presume plus -tion.
entries.definitionCN: 想当然的信念；放肆。它是 presume 加 -tion。

entries.definition: to think something is probably true. It is softer and more conversational than presume.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事可能为真。它比 presume 更软、更口语。

entries.definition: to take something as true without proof. It lacks presume's note of daring or legal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 未经证明即视为真。它没有 presume 的“胆敢”或法律分量。

entries.definition: to be brave enough to do something. It names courage, while presume names overstepping.
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢到敢做某事。它命名勇气，presume 命名越界。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prae- 'before' plus sumere 'take', the presume/assume pair, legal presumption, and the phrase presume on someone.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”、presume 与 assume 这对词、法律推定，以及 presume on someone 这一搭配。

normal.en: Prae- means 'before' and sumere means 'take': presume is to take a belief before you have proof.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”，sumere 意为“取”：presume 就是在有证据之前先取一个信念。

normal.en: Assume is ad- plus sumere, 'take to yourself'; presume is prae- plus sumere, 'take beforehand'. The prefixes tell the difference.
normal.cn: assume 是 ad- 加 sumere，“取到自己身上”；presume 是 prae- 加 sumere，“先取”。前缀说明差别。

normal.en: In law, presumption is a default the other side must attack: presumed innocent until proved guilty.
normal.cn: 法律中，presumption 是一个对方必须攻击的默认值：在被证明有罪前推定无罪。

normal.en: Presume on someone is to take their patience before asking: the debt is real even if no one agreed to it.
normal.cn: presume on someone 是在开口前就先取用对方的耐心：即使没人同意，这笔亏欠也真实存在。

normal.en: Presumably is the everyday adverb: it marks what the speaker thinks is likely but cannot prove.
normal.cn: presumably 是日常副词：标记说话者认为很可能却无法证明的事。

abstract.en: All action starts before certainty: presumption is the credit we extend to the world so that we can move.
abstract.cn: 一切行动都始于确定之前：推定是我们给世界的一笔信用，好让自己能动起来。

abstract.en: The same gesture that lets thought begin can become a social trespass: taking an idea early and taking a person's goodwill early are cousins.
abstract.cn: 让思想得以开始的动作，也可能变成社会越界：提前拿走一个观念，和提前取用一个人的善意，是表亲。

abstract.en: Presumption distributes the burden of proof: whoever presumes forces the other to speak.
abstract.cn: 推定分配证明责任：谁作出推定，谁就迫使对方开口。

examples.en: I presume you have already booked the tickets.
examples.cn: 我想你已经订好票了。

examples.en: The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
examples.cn: 被告在被证明有罪前被推定无罪。

examples.en: He presumed on her patience once too often.
examples.cn: 他仗着她的耐心，终于越过了头。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑米优”——还没熟就先扑上去抓米 → presume 假定、擅自

root: 拉丁语 praesumere“先取”，由 prae-“在前”+ sumere“取”构成；sumere = sub- + emere“取”。与 assume（ad- + sumere）区分。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of presume, all one gesture: taking before. The mind takes a belief before proof; a person takes a step before permission; the law takes a fact before certainty.
sensesIntro.cn: presume 的九个义项，都是同一个动作：先取。心智在证据前取一个信念；人在许可前先迈一步；法律在确定前取一个事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: taking something before you are entitled to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在你尚未获得资格之前就先拿走。

branches.en: SUPPOSE: the mind takes a proposition early and reasons from it.
branches.cn: 假定：心智提前取一个命题并从中推理。

branches.en: HABIT: what is usually true is taken as true again without checking.
branches.cn: 习惯：通常为真的事不再核对就被当作真。

branches.en: LEGAL: the law adopts a default fact so it can act before certainty.
branches.cn: 法律：法律采用默认事实，以便在确定之前行动。

branches.en: DARE: to presume is to act before permission, and the excess has its own adjective.
branches.cn: 胆敢：presume 是在许可前行动，这种越界有专属形容词。

branches.en: EXPLOIT: presuming on a person turns taking-before into taking advantage.
branches.cn: 利用：presume on 某人，把“先取”变成占便宜。

intro.en: Presume is a Latin verb. English adds -tion, -tuous, -tive, and -ably, and the root sumere also builds assume, consume, and resume.
intro.cn: presume 是拉丁动词。英语加 -tion、-tuous、-tive、-ably，词根 sumere 还构成 assume、consume、resume。

latinIntro.en: Latin praesumere 'take before' sits beside assumere 'take to oneself' and sumere 'take up'. The prefix decides the meaning, which is why presume and assume are not interchangeable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praesumere“先取”旁边是 assumere“取到自己身上”与 sumere“取起”。前缀决定含义，所以 presume 与 assume 不可互换。

definition_en: to act as if something is true or real when it is not, or to claim a right or title for yourself
core_image: 一个人抬手在脸前撑起一块看不见的布，把表情挡在后面
scene: 午后的客厅里，孩子把几个靠垫围成一圈，说那是自己的城堡，母亲站在门边没有拆穿。The boy liked to pretend that the cushions were the walls of a castle.
sceneCN: 这里 pretend 是「假装、装作」（第 1 个义项：明知不真，却演得像真的一样）；句意为男孩喜欢假装靠垫就是城堡的墙。图中可辨识物件：围成一圈的靠垫、客厅地毯、站在门边的母亲。

想象中的朋友（儿童虚构的同伴）

senses.title: To act as if something is true when it is not
senses.definition: to behave as if something is true or real while knowing that it is not
senses.definitionCN: 明知某事不真，却表现得像真的一样
senses.example: He pretended to be asleep when his mother opened the door.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲开门时，他假装睡着了。
senses.why: Latin praetendere meant to stretch something out in front of the body, and a made-up manner works exactly like that screen: it stands between you and the people looking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praetendere 本义是「把东西伸到身前」，而装出来的样子正像这样一块挡在身前的帘子，隔开自己和看过来的人，所以「假装」是这个动作最直接的用法。

senses.title: To claim a right or title for oneself
senses.definition: to put forward a claim to a right, title, or quality, often with little support
senses.definitionCN: 对某项权利、头衔或品质提出主张，常缺乏充分依据
senses.example: The young duke pretended to the throne after his uncle died.
senses.exampleCN: 叔父去世后，那位年轻的公爵声称王位应归自己。
senses.why: The oldest sense is holding something out in public and saying it is yours; a claim is that gesture performed with words instead of hands.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把东西当众举起来、说它属于自己；所谓「声称拥有」，就是把这一动作改用言语来完成，手不必真的伸出去。

senses.title: To act out an imagined situation in play
senses.definition: to imagine that a scene is real and act it out, as children do in play
senses.definitionCN: 想象某个情境是真的并把它演出来，如儿童游戏中所为
senses.example: The children pretended that the sofa was a boat on the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把沙发当成一条船，假装在海上航行。
senses.why: Once the word means putting on a show, children's play becomes its natural home, because nothing in the scene has to be true for the scene to work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词等于「演一场戏」，儿童游戏就成了它最自然的场所：布景不必为真，戏照样能演下去，所以「扮演」这一支从「假装」里长出来。

senses.title: Imaginary, used before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that exists only in play or in the imagination
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，形容只存在于游戏或想象中的事物
senses.example: Her daughter invented a pretend friend who lives under the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她女儿虚构了一个住在楼梯下的假想朋友。
senses.why: English often presses a verb into service as a modifier; a scene that is only performed needs a word to mark it as not real, and the bare verb does that job.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动词直接拿来当修饰语；一段只在戏里存在的情境，需要一个词标明它并非真实，而光秃秃的动词正好担起这个差事，于是有了形容词用法。

intro.en: Pretend goes back to a Latin verb for stretching something out in front of you; the modern sense of a false show grew out of that gesture of holding a screen before the body.
intro.cn: pretend 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「把东西伸到身前」的动词；现代「假装」的义项，正是从「在身前撑起遮挡」这个动作长出来的。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front of, and it marks whatever is placed ahead of the body.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，标示被放到身体之前的东西。

items.en: The verb tendere meant to stretch or hold out, and it is the source of a large English family about stretching toward something.
items.cn: 动词 tendere 意为「伸展、伸出」，英语中一大族表示「朝某处伸展」的词都出自它。

items.en: Praetendere joined the two: to stretch something out in front, whether a cloak, an excuse, or a claim.
items.cn: praetendere 把两者合起来：把某物伸到前面，那可以是斗篷，也可以是借口或主张。

items.en: Old French pretendre meant to claim or assert, and English took that meaning over in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pretendre 意为「声称、主张」，英语在十四世纪接受了这个意思。

items.en: From claiming something openly, the word slid toward claiming what is false, and later to children acting out a scene that never happened.
items.cn: 从公开声称某事，词义滑向声称不实之事，后来再指孩子在游戏里演出一段并未发生的情境。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for stretching; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for putting on a false appearance.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「伸展」的动词展开；近义组收其他表示「装出假相」的动词。

entries.definition: A person who claims a title or position that is not theirs.
entries.definitionCN: 声称拥有不属于自己的头衔或地位的人；觊觎者。

entries.definition: A claim to importance or merit that is usually not deserved.
entries.definitionCN: 对重要性或优点的声称，通常并无资格。

entries.definition: A false reason given to hide the real one; it comes from a Latin verb meaning to weave, so it is only close in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 为掩盖真实原因而给出的假理由；它来自表示「编织」的拉丁动词，与本词只是拼写、读音接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To make something false look real, or such a thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 让假的东西看起来像真的，也指这样的假货。

entries.definition: To pretend to have a feeling or an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 假装有某种感受或疾病；佯称。

entries.definition: To imitate the appearance or conditions of something.

entries.definition: To pretend to be someone else, usually in order to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 假扮成别人，通常为了欺骗。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of place and a verb of stretching, and its family keeps returning to what is held out in front of a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀和表示「伸展」的动词构成，同族词都围绕「伸到人前的东西」展开。

normal.en: Praetendere literally means to stretch something out in front, so the oldest picture is a screen held before the body.
normal.cn: praetendere 字面就是「把东西伸到前面」，最古老的画面是一块挡在身前的帘子。

normal.en: Tendere, the stretching verb, also gives extend, intend and tension, all of them about pulling or holding out.
normal.cn: 表示伸展的 tendere 还给出 extend、intend、tension，都跟拉长、伸出有关。

normal.en: Pretense is the noun of the same family: the false front itself rather than the act of putting it up.
normal.cn: pretense 是同一词族的名词，指那层假门面本身，而不是撑起门面的动作。

normal.en: Pretender keeps the older sense of claiming: a person who says a title belongs to them.
normal.cn: pretender 保留了「声称」的旧义：一个说某个头衔属于自己的人。

normal.en: The adjective pretend sits before a noun, as in pretend play, because it labels a whole scene rather than describing an action.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 pretend 站在名词前，如 pretend play，因为它标注的是一整段情境，而不是描述动作。

abstract.en: A screen in front of the body explains both branches: you hide behind it, and you also point to it as proof.
abstract.cn: 身前的帘子能解释两条分支：你躲在它后面，也指着它当凭证。

abstract.en: Pretending is not quite lying, because both sides may know the scene is invented.
abstract.cn: 假装不完全是说谎，因为双方可能都知道这场情境是编出来的。

abstract.en: Children do openly what adults do carefully: build a world, then live in it for an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 孩子把大人小心做的事公开做出来：搭起一个世界，然后整个下午住在里面。
