definition_zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服
definition_en: to be widespread or dominant, to win out over opposition, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下
scene: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下。Westerly winds prevail over the pass for most of the year.
sceneCN: 这里指风与天气长期占主导（第 1 个义项：风与天气盛行）；句意为西风一年中大部分时间控制着这个山口。图中可辨识物件：山口、旧旗、旗杆、被风压弯的草；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「盛行的；普遍的」
由「盛行」的形容词加名词尾构成，义为「盛行；普遍程度」
由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「占优势的；盛行的」
由「占优势的」形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「占优势地」
与拉丁语「valere」同族，经法语进入英语，义为「有用；有帮助」

senses.title: Of wind and weather
senses.definition: to blow steadily or to be the usual weather of a place and season
senses.definitionCN: 指风持续地吹，或成为某地某季的常况
senses.example: Dry winds prevail across the plateau in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季高原上盛行干燥的风。
senses.why: The earliest English uses describe forces that hold the air, because prevailing is first about what dominates a place.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的用法描述控制空气的力量，因为「盛行」首先指在某地占主导。

senses.title: Of customs and ideas
senses.definition: to be widely found or generally accepted among a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中广泛存在或被普遍接受
senses.example: The custom still prevails in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然盛行。
senses.why: Once a usage holds a region the way weather does, the verb extends from air to habit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一种做法像天气那样占住一个地区，这个动词就从空气扩展到习惯。

senses.title: To win an argument
senses.definition: to prove stronger than the opposing case in a debate or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论或争执中证明比对方的主张更强
senses.example: Common sense prevailed after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，常理占了上风。
senses.why: Being stronger is the core of the Latin verb, and an argument is a contest of strength between claims.
senses.whyCN: 「更强」是拉丁动词的核心，而争论正是各种主张之间的力量较量。

senses.title: To win a contest
senses.definition: to defeat opponents in a match, a race or a struggle
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞速或斗争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side prevailed in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在最后几分钟取胜。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal and military verb for the side that turns out stronger.
senses.whyCN: 体育界借用了这个法律与军事动词，指最终更强的一方。

senses.title: To persuade someone
senses.definition: to bring someone round to a course of action by argument or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 通过论证或请求使某人接受某种做法
senses.example: She prevailed on the committee to reopen the case.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服委员会重新审理此案。
senses.why: Persuasion is winning a person over, so the preposition on marks the one who is overcome.
senses.whyCN: 说服就是把一个人争取过来，因此搭配的介词标出被说服的那一方。

senses.title: Of effort that succeeds at last
senses.definition: to succeed after sustained pressure, patience or repeated attempts
senses.definitionCN: 在持续施压、耐心等待或反复尝试之后取得成功
senses.example: Patience and evidence finally prevailed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心与证据最终奏效。
senses.why: The verb can name an impersonal force that wins, even when no person is doing the winning.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以指一种非人的力量取胜，即使并没有人在取胜。

senses.title: Of an old rule that outlives its reason
senses.titleCN: 旧制度延续而缘由已失
senses.definition: to remain in force long after the purpose it once served has disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 在当初的用途消失很久之后仍然有效
senses.example: The old rule still prevails long after its purpose vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧规定在用途消失很久后仍然有效。
senses.why: What prevails simply holds its ground, whether or not anyone can still explain why.
senses.whyCN: 「盛行」的东西只是守住自己的位置，不管还有没有人能解释缘由。

senses.title: To win in a court of law
senses.definition: to succeed in a legal action or to establish a right against the other party
senses.definitionCN: 在法律诉讼中成功，或对另一方确立一项权利
senses.example: The tenant prevailed in the housing dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 租户在住房纠纷中胜诉。
senses.why: Legal language keeps the old sense of a stronger claim carrying the day.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言保留了旧义，即更强的主张最终获胜。

intro.en: Prevail comes from Latin prae-, before or beyond, and valere, to be strong or to be worth, forming praevalere, to be stronger. English took it through French in the fourteenth century; the family of valere also includes valid, value and avail.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语前缀「prae-」「在前、超出」与「valere」「强、有价值」，合成「praevalere」「更强」。英语于十四世纪经法语引入；「valere」的同族词还包括「valid」「value」「avail」。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and it described health, power and value alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为强壮或有价值，同时描述健康、力量与价值。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or beyond, marking a position ahead of others.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前」或「超出」，标出比别人更靠前的位置。

items.en: Prae plus valere gave praevalere, to be stronger, whose past stem is praevaluī.
items.cn: 前缀加动词得到「praevalere」「更强」，其过去词干为「praevaluī」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English, where it was spelled and pronounced in several ways before settling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带到英语，其拼写与读音经过几种形式才固定下来。

items.en: English used prevail first for holding power or influence, and soon for winning a contest.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词表示掌握权力或影响力，很快也用于表示在较量中获胜。

items.en: Courts fixed the sense of winning a case, while ordinary speech kept the weather, custom and persuasion senses.
items.cn: 法庭固定了「胜诉」义，而日常口语保留了天气、习俗与说服诸义。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like prevail; the second group names neighbouring ideas of dominance, victory and persuasion.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「prevail」相近；第二组是与「支配、取胜、说服」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is dominant or most common, as in the prevailing wind.
entries.definitionCN: 指占主导或最常见的形容词，如盛行风。

entries.definition: Widespread in a place or at a time, often used of diseases or beliefs.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地某时广泛存在的，常用于疾病或观念。

entries.definition: The fact or degree of being widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在的事实或程度。

entries.definition: To be useful or helpful; it shares the Latin strength word.
entries.definitionCN: 指有用、有帮助；共用同一个拉丁「强」词。

entries.definition: Bravery in battle, from the same Latin word for strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指战斗中的勇猛，出自同一个表示力量的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To hold the most power or influence in a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地或某种情境中掌握最大的权力或影响。

entries.definition: To be the largest or most noticeable element among others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在其他要素中数量最多或最显著。

entries.definition: To win a decisive victory, often with a sense of celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 指取得决定性胜利，常带庆祝意味。

entries.definition: To convince someone to believe or do something.
entries.definitionCN: 指说服某人相信或去做某事。

entries.definition: To continue in existence or action, close to the sense of an old rule still holding.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续存在或继续行动，接近旧规定仍然有效那一义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin strength word behind prevail, its real family and its fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后表示「强」的拉丁词、真实同族词与固定搭配。

normal.en: Praemia and prevail share a Latin idea: the stronger thing stands, and the stronger claim wins.
normal.cn: 奖品与盛行共享一个拉丁观念：更强的东西站住，更强的主张获胜。

normal.en: The prefix means before or beyond, and the stem means strong, so prevail is to be stronger than what stands in front.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在前、超出」，词干意为「强」，所以这个词指比挡在前面的东西更强。

normal.en: Prevail on someone is the fixed pattern for persuasion, with the preposition on before the person.
normal.cn: 劝说某人用的是固定模式，介词放在人前面。

normal.en: The prevailing wind is the weather phrase, and it is the oldest kind of use.
normal.cn: 盛行风是天气方面的说法，也是最古老的一类用法。

normal.en: Valid, value and avail all descend from the same Latin word for being strong or worth something.
normal.cn: 有效的、价值与有用都出自同一个表示「强或有价值」的拉丁词。

abstract.en: Prevailing is not shouting loudest; it is being the thing that is still standing when the wind drops.
abstract.cn: 盛行不是喊得最响，而是风停之后仍然立着的那一个。

abstract.en: An old rule prevails because nobody remembers how to remove it, not because it is right.
abstract.cn: 旧规定之所以延续，是因为没人记得怎样废除它，而不是因为它正确。

abstract.en: To prevail is to make the world agree with you without having to raise your voice.
abstract.cn: 占上风是让世界同意你，而不必提高嗓门。

examples.en: Cooler air will prevail over the region by the weekend.
examples.cn: 到周末，较凉的空气将控制这一地区。

examples.en: The older interpretation prevailed among historians for a century.
examples.cn: 较旧的解释在历史学家中盛行了整整一个世纪。

examples.en: They tried to prevail on the minister to change the policy.
examples.cn: 他们试图说服部长改变这项政策。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from wind holding a place, to a custom being widespread, an argument or contest won, a person persuaded, effort succeeding, an old rule surviving, and a case won in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从风占住一地，走向习俗广布、争论或较量取胜、说服某人、努力奏效、旧制度延续，以及法律上胜诉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag that bends in a steady gale but never falls, because the stronger force holds its ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面旗在稳定的大风里被压弯却从不倒下，因为更强的力量守住了位置。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: one wind or one kind of weather holds a place for most of the year.
branches.cn: 天气：一种风或一类天气在一年的大部分时间里占住一个地方。

branches.en: THE LONG HABIT: a custom spreads widely, and an old rule stays after its reason is gone.
branches.cn: 长久的习惯：习俗广泛流传，旧规定在缘由消失后仍留下。

branches.en: THE STRONGER CLAIM: an argument wins out, and a side wins the match.
branches.cn: 更强的主张：一种论点占上风，一方赢下比赛。

branches.en: THE OVERCOMING: a person is persuaded, and patient effort succeeds at last.
branches.cn: 争取与奏效：一个人被说服，耐心的努力最终成功。

branches.en: THE COURT: the stronger legal right carries the case.
branches.cn: 法庭：更强的法律权利赢得案件。

intro.en: Prevail is a Latin verb built from a prefix of position and a stem of strength, and English keeps both pieces in a whole family.
intro.cn: 这是一个由位置前缀与力量词干构成的拉丁动词，英语在两个成分上都保留了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere supplies the strength, prae- supplies the advantage, and praevalere joins them into one verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「valere」提供力量，「prae-」提供优势，「praevalere」把两者合成一个动词。

items.meaning: to be strong, to be worth
items.example: The stem carries health, power and worth together.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干同时带着健康、力量与价值。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English shortened the Latin verb into its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个拉丁动词缩短成现代形态。

items.example: It describes the wind or the mood of a time.
items.exampleCN: 它描述风或一个时期的风气。

items.example: Epidemiologists measure it as a rate.

definition_zh: 阻止；防止；使无法；妨碍；预防
definition_en: to stop something from happening, or to make it impossible for someone to do something
core_image: 有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在门框上把路挡住
scene: 雨天路滑，小区门口新铺了一道减速带，旁边立着一块提示牌。The speed bump was installed to prevent accidents at the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 prevent 是「预防、防止发生」（第 3 个义项：采取措施，使事故一类的事不发生）；句意为这道减速带是为了防止门口发生事故而设。图中可辨识景物：减速带、雨后的路面、提示牌。

pos.zh: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍

derivatives.zh: 由 prevent 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「阻止；预防」
由 prevent 加 -ive 构成，义为「预防的；防护的」
由 prevent 加 -able 构成，义为「可预防的；可以避免的」

senses.title: To stop an event from taking place
senses.definition: to stop an event or action before it can happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件或行动来不及发生
senses.example: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
senses.exampleCN: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。
senses.why: Latin praevenire meant to come before someone; arriving at a place first is what lets you stand in the way of what follows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevenire 意为「先于某人到来」，先一步赶到某处，才有机会挡在后头那件事的前面，所以「阻止」是「先来」的直接结果。

senses.title: To make it impossible for someone to act
senses.titleCN: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍
senses.definition: to make it impossible for someone to do what they intended
senses.definitionCN: 使某人无法做成原本打算做的事
senses.example: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。
senses.why: Here no force is aimed at the person; the word only reports that an obstacle got there first and the action never began.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不对某人施加力量，只是说明障碍先到了，那个动作始终没能开始，所以介词 from 后面接的是被挡住的行动。

senses.title: To reduce the risk of illness or damage
senses.definition: to take action so that illness, damage, or trouble does not develop
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施，使疾病、损害或麻烦不致发展起来
senses.example: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。
senses.why: Medicine widened the focus from one event to a whole class of risk: acting early becomes a habit rather than a single block in a doorway.
senses.whyCN: 医学把焦点从单一事件扩大成一整类风险：提前动手变成习惯，而不再是门口一次性的拦阻，于是「预防」从「阻止」里独立出来。

senses.title: To go before, in older religious language
senses.definition: to go before or act ahead of someone, a sense kept mainly in old prayers
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人之前或先行行动，这一义项主要保留在古老祷词中
senses.example: The old prayer asks God to prevent us in all our doings.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老祷词祈求上帝在我们一切所行的事上先行引导。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin meaning surviving in English; modern usage narrowed the word, but the prayer book never changed.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义在英语里的遗留：字面上就是「走在前面」。现代用法把词义收窄了，祷词却一直没改，所以这个古老义项仍能读到。

intro.en: Prevent is built from a Latin prefix meaning before and the verb to come: to prevent is, quite literally, to get there first, and hindering grew out of that head start.
intro.cn: prevent 由表示「在前」的拉丁前缀与动词「来」构成：字面上就是「先到一步」；阻挡的义项，正是从这个抢先到达的动作长出来的。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that appears in predict and prepare.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，predict 与 prepare 也用了这个前缀。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it supplies the ven- seen in intervene, convene and event.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，intervene、convene、event 里的 ven- 都来自它。

items.en: Praevenire meant to come before someone, to arrive ahead of them, and so to anticipate or forestall.
items.cn: praevenire 意为「先于某人来到」，即赶在对方前头到达，因此引申为预先、抢先拦下。

items.en: Old French prevenir kept both the sense of arriving first and the sense of hindering by getting there early.
items.cn: 古法语 prevenir 同时保留「先到」与「因先到而阻挡」两层意思。

items.en: Modern English dropped the literal meaning and kept the result: something is prevented when it never gets to happen.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了字面上的「先到」，只留下结果：一件事始终没能发生，就是被 prevent 了。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for coming; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for blocking, avoiding and putting off harm.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「来」的动词展开；近义组收阻挡、避开与消解祸患的动词。

entries.definition: The act of stopping something before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前将其阻止的行为；预防。

entries.definition: Intended to stop illness or trouble before it starts.
entries.definitionCN: 意在疾病或麻烦开始前就加以阻止的；预防性的。

entries.definition: Able to be stopped before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 可以在发生前被阻止的；可预防的。

entries.definition: Coming before or anticipating something; used mainly in theology.
entries.definitionCN: 先于某事先行而来的；主要用于神学语境。

entries.definition: To keep away from something so that it does not happen to you.
entries.definitionCN: 远远避开某物，使它不落到自己身上。

entries.definition: To make progress or action difficult.
entries.definitionCN: 使进展或行动变得困难。

entries.definition: To turn something bad away before it arrives.
entries.definitionCN: 在坏事到来之前把它挡开。

entries.definition: To make someone decide not to act, usually through fear of the consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 使人因后果的威慑而决定不做某事。

entries.definition: To end an action that has already started.
entries.definitionCN: 使已经开始的动作停止。

normalIntro.en: The word puts a Latin prefix meaning before onto the verb to come, and its family keeps the picture of arriving first.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在表示「来」的拉丁动词前加上「在前」的前缀，同族词都保留着「先一步到达」的画面。

normal.en: Prae- plus venire: prevent is to come before, and only later to block because you got there first.
normal.cn: prae- 加 venire：prevent 本是「先来」，后来才因先到而挡住。

normal.en: The ven- of prevent means come, as in invent and convene; pretend has a different verb, tendere, meaning stretch, so the two share only the prefix.
normal.cn: prevent 里的 ven- 意为「来」，invent、convene 同此；pretend 用的是另一个动词 tendere（伸展），两词只共享前缀，词源并不相同。

normal.en: Prevention is the noun and preventive the adjective; both name stopping something ahead of time.
normal.cn: prevention 是名词，preventive 是形容词，两者都指提前挡住。

normal.en: Preventable marks what can be stopped, with the same -able heard in avoidable and curable.
normal.cn: preventable 标注「拦得住的」，后缀 -able 与 avoidable、curable 里的相同。

normal.en: The pattern「prevent somebody from doing something」keeps the image of a body standing in another person's way.
normal.cn: 搭配「prevent somebody from doing something」保留了「一个人挡在另一个人路上」的画面。

abstract.en: To prevent is to win a race nobody watches: the best prevention leaves nothing to see afterwards.
abstract.cn: prevent 是赢下一场没人观看的比赛：最好的预防，事后什么也看不见。

abstract.en: The word once meant arrive first, and every act of prevention is still a small race against an event.
abstract.cn: 这个词原本只表示「先到」，而每一次预防，仍是在和某个事件抢时间。

abstract.en: Prevent and pretend share a prefix but not a road: one comes first, the other stretches a screen.
abstract.cn: prevent 与 pretend 共享前缀，却不同路：一个抢先赶到，一个撑起帘子。

examples.en: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
examples.cn: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。

examples.en: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
examples.cn: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。

examples.en: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
examples.cn: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「扑来问」——人还没进门就先扑上去问一句，顺势把人拦在门外。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ venire（来）构成 praevenire，本义「先来、抢先到达」，引申为「预先阻挡」，经古法语 prevenir 进入英语。ve-nire 是「来」，与 pretend 所用的 tendere（伸展）不同源，两词只共享前缀 prae-。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arriving before something else; the senses run from stopping an event, to blocking a person, to forestalling illness, and finally to the old literal sense of going before.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「赶在某事之前到达」；义项从阻止事件，到挡住某人，到防病于未然，最后回到古老的「先行」本义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm raised across a doorway a moment before someone reaches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在那里。

branches.en: a hand shutting the window before the rain starts
branches.cn: 雨还没下，一只手先把窗关上

branches.en: a guard standing in a doorway with arms spread
branches.cn: 守卫张开手臂站在门口

branches.en: a needle given before the season of flu
branches.cn: 流感季节来临前打的一针

branches.en: an old prayer asking to be led from the front
branches.cn: 古老祷词求人先行引领

branches.en: a speed bump slowing every car at the gate
branches.cn: 减速带让门口每辆车都慢下来

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix of place to a Latin verb of coming, then adds English endings that name the act, the quality and the possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示位置的拉丁前缀与表示「来」的拉丁动词结合，再加上命名行为、性质与可能性的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 预防性的；预防的；预防措施
definition_en: intended to stop something from happening, or a measure taken for that purpose
core_image: 一辆检修车停在铁路边，轨道还没裂，工人已经在换那根旧螺栓
scene: 预防性检查在桥投入使用之前就发现了裂缝。Preventive checks caught the crack before the bridge was used.
sceneCN: 这里 preventive 是「预防性的」（第 1 个义项：为阻止事情发生而做的）；句意：预防性检查在桥梁启用之前就发现了裂缝。图中可辨识物件：检修车、尚未裂开的轨道、换下的旧螺栓；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Serving to stop something
senses.definition: designed or intended to stop an unwanted event before it occurs
senses.definitionCN: 旨在在不受欢迎的事件发生之前将其阻止
senses.example: The school installed preventive barriers at the stairwell.
senses.exampleCN: 学校在楼梯口安装了预防性护栏。
senses.why: The -ive suffix marks function. Preventive describes what a measure is for, not what it has already done.
senses.whyCN: -ive 后缀标记功能。preventive 描述措施“为了什么”，而不是“已经做了什么”。

senses.title: Preventive medicine
senses.definition: the branch of medicine concerned with avoiding disease rather than treating it
senses.definitionCN: 关注避免疾病而非治疗疾病的医学分支
senses.example: Preventive medicine focuses on vaccination and screening.
senses.exampleCN: 预防医学侧重疫苗接种与筛查。
senses.why: Medicine splits by timing. Preventive work happens while the patient is well, which is why it is a separate branch.
senses.whyCN: 医学按时机分工。预防工作发生在病人还健康时，因此成为独立分支。

senses.title: Preventive measures
senses.titleCN: 预防措施：提前做的那几件事
senses.definition: countable steps taken in advance to reduce a risk
senses.definitionCN: 为降低风险而提前采取的可数步骤
senses.example: The report lists ten preventive measures for the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 报告为这家工厂列出十项预防措施。
senses.why: As a noun the word names concrete items, so a policy becomes a checklist of steps rather than a principle.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时它命名具体条目，于是政策变成一张步骤清单，而非一条原则。

senses.title: Preventive war
senses.titleCN: 预防性战争：趁对方还没强起来
senses.definition: describing war launched to stop an opponent from becoming a future threat, distinct from preemptive war
senses.definitionCN: 描述为阻止对手成为未来威胁而发动的战争，区别于先发制人的战争
senses.example: Preventive war is illegal under the modern law of conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 依据现代冲突法，预防性战争是非法的。
senses.why: The distinction is legal and precise: preemptive strikes answer an imminent attack, preventive war answers a distant one.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分是法律性且精确的：先发制人回应迫在眉睫的攻击，预防性战争回应遥远的威胁。

senses.title: Preventive detention
senses.titleCN: 预防性拘留：先关起来防出事
senses.definition: in law, detention ordered to stop a person from committing future harm rather than to punish past acts
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指为防止某人将来造成损害而非惩罚其过去行为的拘留
senses.example: Preventive detention raises serious human rights questions.
senses.exampleCN: 预防性拘留引发严重的人权问题。
senses.why: Law usually punishes the past. Preventive detention acts on the future, which is exactly why it is controversial.
senses.whyCN: 法律通常惩罚过去。预防性拘留作用于未来，这正是它受争议的原因。

senses.title: Preventive maintenance
senses.titleCN: 预防性维护：坏了之前先修
senses.definition: scheduled servicing of equipment based on time or use, before failure occurs
senses.definitionCN: 按时间或使用量在故障发生前安排的设备保养
senses.example: Preventive maintenance is cheaper than emergency repair.
senses.exampleCN: 预防性维护比紧急抢修便宜。
senses.why: Engineering splits maintenance into reactive and preventive. The adjective marks the version that acts before the breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 工程把维护分为事后与预防。这个形容词标记“在故障之前”的那一种。

senses.title: Preventive diplomacy
senses.titleCN: 预防性外交：别让争端打起来
senses.definition: diplomatic action taken to stop a dispute from becoming violent
senses.definitionCN: 为防止争端升级为暴力而采取的外交行动
senses.example: Preventive diplomacy kept the border talks alive.
senses.exampleCN: 预防性外交让边界谈判得以延续。
senses.why: Diplomacy borrows the medical word: conflict is treated like a disease that can be caught early.
senses.whyCN: 外交借用了医学词：冲突被视为一种可以早期发现的疾病。

senses.title: Preventive check
senses.titleCN: 预防性限制：经济思想里的旧词
senses.definition: in historical economics, Malthus's preventive checks are the limits people place on population growth themselves
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学史中，马尔萨斯的“预防性限制”指人们自行对人口增长施加的限制
senses.example: Malthus called delayed marriage a preventive check.
senses.exampleCN: 马尔萨斯把推迟婚姻称为一种预防性限制。
senses.why: The word was used long before medicine made it common, and this economic sense shows its general logic: act on the cause before the effect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在医学让它流行之前就已被使用，这一经济学义显示了它的普遍逻辑：在结果之前作用于原因。

intro.en: Preventive is prevent plus -ive, from Latin praevenire 'to come before, forestall' (prae- 'before' + venire 'come').
intro.cn: preventive 是 prevent 加 -ive，源自拉丁 praevenire“先到、预先拦下”（prae-“在前”+ venire“来”）。

items.en: venire 'to come' underlies the family. Event, invent, intervene and convention all use the same stem with different prefixes.
items.cn: venire“来”是该词族的基础。event、invent、intervene、convention 都用同一词干，配不同前缀。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus venire gives 'to come before'. The practical sense 'to hinder' grows from arriving first.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 venire 得“先到”。由于先到，实用义“拦住”生长出来。

items.en: -ivus in Latin marks capacity or function, so preventive means 'having the function of preventing'.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ivus 标记能力或功能，所以 preventive 意为“具有阻止的功能”。

items.en: English uses preventive first as a noun for a remedy that wards off illness, then as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语最早把 preventive 用作名词，指防病之物，随后用作形容词。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries preventive medicine becomes the name of a whole branch of practice.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，预防医学成为整个实践分支的名称。

items.en: The same adjective spreads to detention, war, maintenance and diplomacy, where the shared point is action before harm.
items.cn: 同一形容词扩展到拘留、战争、维护与外交，共同点是“在损害之前行动”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ven- stem or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group all act early, differing in whether they stop or prepare.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ven- 词干或 pre- 前缀；近义组都提早行动，差别在“阻止”还是“准备”。

entries.definition: the act or policy of stopping something. The noun names the effort; the adjective describes measures.
entries.definitionCN: 预防的行为或政策。名词命名努力，形容词描述措施。

entries.definition: an alternative form of preventive, common in speech and some writing. Both are accepted.
entries.definitionCN: preventive 的变体形式，口语和一些写作中常见，两者都被接受。

entries.definition: acting first against an imminent threat. It comes from pre- plus emere 'buy, take', not from venire.
entries.definitionCN: 先发制人的。来自 pre- 加 emere“买、取”，并非 venire。

entries.definition: describing treatment given to ward off disease. It is the clinical adjective for preventive in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 预防性的。它是医学中 preventive 的临床形容词。

entries.definition: done to avoid possible harm. It stresses caution rather than a systematic programme.
entries.definitionCN: 防范性的。强调谨慎，而非系统性的方案。

entries.definition: describing something that shields from harm. It implies a barrier, while preventive implies earlier action.
entries.definitionCN: 保护性的。暗含屏障，而 preventive 暗含更早的行动。

entries.definition: able to cure a condition already present. It is the natural counterpart of preventive.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗性的。它是 preventive 的天然对照词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: -ive marks function, so preventive means 'doing the job of stopping'.
normal.cn: -ive 标记功能，所以 preventive 意为“承担阻止任务”。

normal.en: Preventive maintenance is the clearest everyday example: repair before the machine breaks.
normal.cn: 预防性维护是最清楚的日常例子：在机器坏之前先修。

normal.en: Preventive versus curative is a timing pair, not a quality pair.
normal.cn: 预防与治疗是一对时机词，不是一对质量词。

normal.en: Preventive war is legally different from preemptive war, and the difference is the distance of the threat.
normal.cn: 预防性战争与先发制人战争在法律上不同，差别在威胁的远近。

normal.en: Preventive detention is controversial precisely because it acts on the future rather than the past.
normal.cn: 预防性拘留之所以有争议，正因为它作用于未来而非过去。

abstract.en: Picture a mechanic replacing a bearing that still turns quietly.
abstract.cn: 想象机械师换下一个仍在安静转动的轴承。

abstract.en: Picture a fence put up while the field is still empty.
abstract.cn: 想象田里还空着时就立起的围栏。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor's appointment scheduled while the patient feels fine.
abstract.cn: 想象病人在感觉良好时预约的那次体检。

examples.en: Preventive treatment reduced the number of severe cases.
examples.cn: 预防性治疗减少了重症病例数。

examples.en: The airline follows a preventive maintenance schedule.
examples.cn: 该航空公司执行预防性维护计划。

examples.en: Preventive steps are cheaper, but they are invisible when they work.
examples.cn: 预防措施更便宜，但奏效时却看不见。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞文提夫”音近 preventive：先“文”住口子、再“提”前防住——提前挡住不让发生 → preventive 预防性的

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ venire“来”→ praevenire“先到、预先拦下”；prevent + -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表功能）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe measures that act before the harm, whether the harm is illness, war, crime or a broken bearing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“在损害之前行动”的措施，无论损害是疾病、战争、犯罪还是坏掉的轴承。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bolt replaced before the rail cracks.
core.cn: 核心意象：轨道裂开之前换下的螺栓。

branches.en: FUNCTION AND ITEMS: the adjective describes the purpose, the countable noun lists the steps.
branches.cn: 功能与条目：形容词描述目的，可数名词列出步骤。

branches.en: MEDICINE: preventive work happens while the patient is well, which defines the branch.
branches.cn: 医学：预防工作发生在病人健康时，这定义了该分支。

branches.en: LAW: preventive war and preventive detention both act on a future harm, which is why both are contested.
branches.cn: 法律：预防性战争与预防性拘留都作用于未来的损害，因此都受争议。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: maintenance before failure is the industrial model of the same logic.
branches.cn: 工程：故障前的维护是同一逻辑的工业模型。

branches.en: SOCIETY: diplomacy and Malthus's checks apply the word to conflict and population.
branches.cn: 社会：外交与马尔萨斯的限制把词用于冲突与人口。

intro.en: Preventive is prevent plus -ive. The base carries 'come before', the suffix marks function, and the noun prevention carries the policy.
intro.cn: preventive 是 prevent 加 -ive。词基携带“先到”，后缀标记功能，名词 prevention 承载政策含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire 'come' → praevenire 'forestall'. English keeps vent- in prevent and adds -ive from -ivus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 venire“来”→ praevenire“预先拦下”。英语在 prevent 中保留 vent-，加 -ive（来自 -ivus）。

items.example: Prevention of sepsis is the priority.
items.exampleCN: 预防败血症是首要任务。

items.meaning: a device that stops a fault

definition_zh: 以前的；先前的；上一个的；以前的（所有者等）
definition_en: existing or happening before something else, especially immediately before
core_image: 一条路上留下的一串脚印：你已经走过的那一段
scene: 会议开始前，主持人先翻开旧纪要。The chair read the minutes of the previous meeting first, so that everyone remembered what had been decided last time.
sceneCN: 这里 previous 是「上一次的、先前的」（第 2 个义项：紧接在这一次之前的那一次）；句意：主持人先读了上一次会议的纪要，让大家记起上次决定了什么。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、旧纪要、日历、文件夹、投影幕；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 以前的；先前的；上一个的
