最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Happening before in time
senses.definition: existing or occurring earlier than something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: Previous studies reached a different conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的研究得出了不同结论。
senses.why: Latin praevius means 'going before', from prae- 'before' and via 'way'. The word pictures something that has already travelled the road you are now on.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevius 意为“走在前面的”，由 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”构成。这个词描绘已经走完你脚下这段路的东西。

senses.title: Immediately preceding
senses.definition: the one directly before the current one
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着当前这个之前的那个
senses.example: The previous chapter explained the method.
senses.exampleCN: 上一章解释了方法。
senses.why: English often uses the word for the nearest predecessor, not any earlier item. The road image narrows to the step just behind your heel.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用它指最近的前一个，而非任何更早的项。道路意象收窄到脚跟后的那一步。

senses.title: Former, no longer current
senses.definition: holding a position or relationship no longer held
senses.definitionCN: 担任的职位或关系已不再持续
senses.example: The previous owner kept the garden beautiful.
senses.exampleCN: 前任主人把花园打理得很美。
senses.why: When attached to a role or person, the word marks a slot that has changed hands. What is previous is not merely earlier but replaced.
senses.whyCN: 当它附着于角色或人时，标记一个已经易手的槽位。previous 不只是更早，而是已被取代。

senses.title: Earlier in a sequence or order
senses.definition: coming earlier in an ordered series
senses.definitionCN: 在有序序列中更早出现
senses.example: Check the previous entry in the log.
senses.exampleCN: 检查日志中的前一条。
senses.why: Sequences let 'before' be counted: the previous item is the one at index n-1. The spatial image of the road becomes an ordered list.
senses.whyCN: 序列让“在前”可以计数：previous 项就是索引 n-1 的那一项。道路的空间意象变成有序列表。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase previous to
senses.definition: in formal usage, earlier than or before
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：早于、在……之前
senses.example: Previous to 1900, the town had no railway.
senses.exampleCN: 1900 年以前，这个镇没有铁路。
senses.why: The phrase turns the adjective into a preposition. It is more formal than 'before' and slightly archaic in speech, but common in legal and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把形容词变成介词。它比 before 正式，口语中略古旧，但在法律与历史写作中常见。

senses.title: Premature or hasty (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, happening too soon, before the proper time
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：发生得过早，早于适当时间
senses.example: a previous conclusion, drawn before the evidence
senses.exampleCN: 证据未齐就作出的过早结论
senses.why: The word once carried the sense 'too early', not only 'earlier'. The Latin comparative idea of going ahead could imply jumping the gun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾有“过早”而非仅仅“更早”的意思。拉丁语“走在前面”的比较意味，可以暗指抢跑。

senses.title: The antecedent term (logic)
senses.definition: in logic, the premise or term that comes before another
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中先于另一项的前提或词项
senses.example: The previous proposition must be established first.
senses.exampleCN: 前一个命题必须先被确立。
senses.why: Logic orders propositions in a chain. The previous proposition is the ground on which the next stands, so priority becomes inference.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把命题排成链。前一个命题是后一个站立的地面，于是“在先”变成推理关系。

senses.title: Already mentioned or known
senses.definition: already referred to earlier in a text or conversation
senses.definitionCN: 在文本或谈话中已被提及
senses.example: The previous example shows the pattern clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 前面的例子清楚展示了这个模式。
senses.why: Reference needs a backward pointer. The word tells the reader to look up the road already travelled, which is why it is so common in academic prose.
senses.whyCN: 指称需要一个向后指的箭头。这个词让读者回望已经走过的路，所以它在学术写作中如此常见。

intro.en: Previous is a road word: Latin praevius 'going before' combines prae- 'before' with via 'way'. English borrowed it in the 17c. and made it the ordinary adjective for the step just behind.
intro.cn: previous 是一个道路词：拉丁语 praevius“走在前面的”把 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”结合。英语在 17 世纪借入，并让它成为指“刚过去那一步”的常用形容词。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English with the sense 'going before in time or order'.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早在英语中记录为“在时间或次序上在前”之义。

items.en: From Latin praevius 'leading the way, going before' = prae- 'before' + via 'way, road'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 praevius“引路、走在前”= prae-“在前”+ via“道路”。

items.en: via also yields deviate, obvious, trivial, convey, and voyage. The family is about roads, and 'before on the road' is the core of previous.
items.cn: via 还生成 deviate、obvious、trivial、convey、voyage。这个词族关乎道路，而“路上在前”正是 previous 的核心。

items.en: The word settles into its modern sense, especially 'the one immediately before'.
items.cn: 这个词稳定在现代义，尤其指“紧接在前的那一个”。

items.en: The prepositional phrase previous to becomes common in formal prose in the 18c.
items.cn: 介词短语 previous to 在 18 世纪正式书面语中变得常见。

items.en: Modern English prefers before in speech and keeps previous to for legal and historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语口语偏好 before，法律与历史写作保留 previous to。

note.en: The first group shares the via or -vious shape; the second is about adjectives that also mean earlier.
note.cn: 第一组共享 via 或 -vious 的形态，第二组看同样表示“更早”的形容词。

entries.definition: at an earlier time. It is previous plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以前；先前。它是 previous 加 -ly。

entries.definition: clear, literally 'in the way'. It uses the same via.
entries.definitionCN: 明显的，字面“挡在路上”。它用同一个 via。

entries.definition: to go off the way. It is de- 'away from' + via.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离道路。它是 de-“离开”+ via。

entries.definition: earlier or more important. It is stronger and more formal than previous.
entries.definitionCN: 更早或更重要的。它比 previous 更强、更正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past holder of a role. It contrasts with 'latter'.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或某角色的前任。它与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming just before in order. It is the precise word for the item at n-1.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它是指 n-1 项的确切词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin via 'road', the praevius image of going before, the previous/prior/former trio, and the phrase previous to.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 via“道路”、praevius“走在前面”的意象、previous/prior/former 三词的区别，以及短语 previous to。

normal.en: Via means 'road'. Previous things have already walked the road you are on.
normal.cn: via 意为“道路”。previous 的东西已经走过你脚下的路。

normal.en: Prae- means 'before'. Put the two together and you get 'going before on the way'.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”。两者相加就是“在路上走在前面”。

normal.en: Previous vs prior: previous is the everyday 'last one'; prior is formal and can also mean 'more important'.
normal.cn: previous 与 prior：previous 是日常的“上一个”，prior 更正式，还可表示“更重要”。

normal.en: Previous vs former: former contrasts with latter in a pair; previous can point to any earlier item.
normal.cn: previous 与 former：former 在一对中与 latter 相对；previous 可指任何更早的项。

normal.en: Previous to is a formal preposition: lawyers and historians use it, everyday speech says before.
normal.cn: previous to 是正式介词：律师与历史学家用它，日常口语说 before。

abstract.en: Memory is the road behind us: to call something previous is to locate it on that road, not merely to date it.
abstract.cn: 记忆是我们身后的路：称某物 previous，就是把它定位在那条路上，而不只是给它标日期。

abstract.en: Every present moment defines its predecessor, so 'previous' is a relational word disguised as a time word.
abstract.cn: 每个当下都在定义它的前一刻，所以 previous 是一个伪装成时间词的关系词。

abstract.en: The past is not one thing: previous, former, and prior cut it differently, by nearness, role, and rank.
abstract.cn: 过去不是一整块：previous、former、prior 按近远、角色与等级把它切成不同的段。

examples.en: The previous meeting lasted three hours.
examples.cn: 上一次会议开了三个小时。

examples.en: She had no previous experience in teaching.
examples.cn: 她此前没有教学经验。

examples.en: Previous to that year, the village had no school.
examples.cn: 在那一年之前，这个村子没有学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞威士”——扑向前一个瑞威士（路标）→ previous 先前的、上一个

root: 拉丁语 praevius“走在前面的”，由 prae-“在前”+ via“道路”构成；同族有 deviate、obvious、trivial、convey。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of previous, all placed on a road behind the present. The road can be time (last year), a list (the item before), a role (the former owner), or a text (the example above).
sensesIntro.cn: previous 的八个义项都放在当下身后的一条路上。这条路可以是时间（去年）、列表（前一项）、角色（前任）或文本（上面的例子）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the stretch of road already walked.
core.cn: 核心意象：已经走过的那一段路。

branches.en: BEFORE: earlier in time, with an archaic note of 'too early'.
branches.cn: 在前：时间上更早，古义带“过早”色彩。

branches.en: JUST BEFORE: the nearest predecessor in a sequence or list.
branches.cn: 紧邻在前：序列或列表中最近的前一项。

branches.en: FORMER: a role or owner that has been replaced.
branches.cn: 前任：已被取代的角色或所有者。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: previous to turns the adjective into a formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：previous to 把形容词变成正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: REFERENCE: in logic and texts, the earlier item grounds or points back.
branches.cn: 指称：在逻辑与文本中，前项提供依据或向后指。

intro.en: Previous is an adjective from Latin praevius. English adds -ly and -ness, and the same via builds deviate, obvious, and convey.
intro.cn: previous 是来自拉丁 praevius 的形容词。英语加 -ly 与 -ness，同一个 via 还构成 deviate、obvious、convey。

latinIntro.en: Latin praevius 'going before' combines prae- 'before' with via 'way'. The via family is large: deviate, obvious, trivial, convey, voyage. All keep the image of a road.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praevius“走在前”把 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”结合。via 词族很大：deviate、obvious、trivial、convey、voyage。它们都保留道路意象。

items.meaning: to leave the road; to depart from a norm
a departure from a route or standard

items.structure: from Old French voiage, from via
items.meaning: a journey by sea or space

definition_zh: 以前；先前；此前；前面提到的
definition_en: at an earlier time, either before now or before a past moment that has already been mentioned
core_image: 行路人回头看向身后那条已经走过的路，路的尽头是旧日的景象
scene: 她翻看旧合同时才发现，这间屋子最早并不是办公室。The room had previously been used as a storeroom.
sceneCN: 这里 previously 是「此前、在那之前」（第 2 个义项：在已经提到的某个过去时间点之前）；句意为这间屋子此前曾被用作储藏室。图中可辨识物件：摊开的旧合同、空荡的房间、墙角的纸箱。

pos.zh: （书面）前面提到的；先前所述的

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 即得形容词 previous，义为「以前的；先前的」
由 previous 加介词 to 构成的固定说法，用作介词，义为「在……之前」

senses.title: At a time before now
senses.definition: at some time in the past, seen from the point of view of the present
senses.definitionCN: 站在现在回看，事情发生在过去某个时候
senses.example: The shop was previously a bank.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店以前是一家银行。
senses.why: Latin praevius described what goes before on a road; time is pictured the same way, with earlier events lying further back along it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevius 描述路上走在前面的东西；时间也被这样设想，更早的事就留在路更靠后的位置，所以「以前」是这个词最朴素的用法。

senses.title: Before a particular moment in the past
senses.definition: before an earlier point in time that is already being talked about
senses.definitionCN: 在已经提到的某个过去时间点之前
senses.example: She had previously worked in the same office for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 她此前在同一间办公室工作过十年。
senses.why: The same word can serve a second reference point; English marks the extra distance back with the past perfect instead of coining a new adverb.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能为第二个参照点服务；英语用过去完成时来标示这多出来的一段距离，而不另造一个新副词。

senses.title: Mentioned earlier in a text
senses.titleCN: （书面）前面提到的；先前所述的
senses.definition: used to refer to something already stated earlier in a text or a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 用来指文章或谈话中已经说过的内容
senses.example: The previously described method works only on small samples.
senses.exampleCN: 前面描述的那种方法只适用于小样本。
senses.why: Writing puts words in a line, so what came before on the page is read as what came before in time; the adverb simply points backwards along that line.
senses.whyCN: 书写把词排成一行，纸面上先出现的内容就被读成时间上先出现的内容，这个副词只是沿着那一行往后指一指。

intro.en: Previously is an English ending added to previous, a word built in Latin from before plus way: the earlier thing is the one further back along the road.
intro.cn: previously 是在 previous 后面加英语副词词尾构成的，而 previous 在拉丁语里由「在前」与「路」组合而成：更早的事，就是留在路更后方的那一段。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, and here it marks what lies ahead on a road.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，这里标示路上位于前面的东西。

items.en: Via meant way or road, and it is also the source of trivial, deviate and obviate.
items.cn: via 意为「路、道路」，trivial、deviate、obviate 也都出自它。

items.en: Praevious described someone or something going before, leading the way, or placed in front.
items.cn: praevius 形容走在前面、带路或位于前方的人或物。

items.en: English formed previous from that Latin adjective; it is first recorded in the seventeenth century, though the exact decade is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用这个拉丁形容词造出 previous；一般认为它最早见于十七世纪，具体年代尚不确定。

items.en: Adding -ly makes an adverb, and the same ending turns a position on a road into a position in time.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 构成副词，同一个词尾把「在路上的位置」转成了「时间上的先后」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin word for road or the prefix meaning before; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs that point to an earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「路」的拉丁词或表示「在前」的前缀；近义组收指向更早时间的副词。

entries.definition: Coming or happening before the one mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 在提到的那一个之前的；先前的。

entries.definition: Allowing water or light to pass through; it uses the same road word with per-, through.
entries.definitionCN: 可让水或光透过的；它与 previous 共用表示「路」的词根，前缀 per- 意为「穿过」，只是拼写接近。

entries.definition: Not letting anything pass through, or not affected by something.
entries.definitionCN: 任何东西都透不过的；也指不受某事物影响。

entries.definition: The ability to see what will happen; its second element comes from a verb meaning to see, not from the word for road.
entries.definitionCN: 预见未来的能力；后半部分来自表示「看」的动词，而非表示「路」的词，与本词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In an earlier period, when things were different.
entries.definitionCN: 在早先某个时期，当时情况与现在不同。

entries.definition: At a time before the one being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 在所讨论的时间之前。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, without naming the exact point.
entries.definitionCN: 在更早的时候，不点明具体时点。

entries.definition: Up to this time, used mostly in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 直到此时为止，多用于书面语。

entries.definition: At some time in the past, as in a once-famous singer.
entries.definitionCN: 在过去某个时候，如「曾经出名的歌手」。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin word for road with a prefix meaning before, plus an English ending that turns it into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「路」的词加上表示「在前」的前缀，再加一个英语副词词尾。

normal.en: Prae- plus via: previous is literally what is ahead on the road, and then what is earlier in time.
normal.cn: prae- 加 via：previous 字面上是「路上在前面的」，再转成时间上更早的。

normal.en: The same via gives deviate, to turn off the road, and obviate, to clear the road away.
normal.cn: 同一个 via 还给出 deviate（离开道路）与 obviate（把路清掉）。

normal.en: Previously is simply previous plus -ly, the ending that turns an adjective into an adverb of time or manner.
normal.cn: previously 就是 previous 加 -ly，这个词尾把形容词变成表示时间或方式的副词。

normal.en: Per- means through, so pervious describes something water can pass through; previous and pervious differ by one letter.
normal.cn: per- 意为「穿过」，所以 pervious 形容水能穿过的物体；previous 与 pervious 只差一个字母。

normal.en: In a paragraph, previously points back to what has already been said, which is the stretch of road already walked.
normal.cn: 在段落里，previously 指向已经说过的内容，也就是已经走过的那段路。

abstract.en: Time is treated as a road here: what is behind you is earlier, what is ahead is later.
abstract.cn: 这里把时间当成一条路：身后的更早，前面的更晚。

abstract.en: One letter separates previous from pervious, and one prefix separates going before from passing through.
abstract.cn: 一个字母隔开 previous 与 pervious，一个前缀隔开「走在前面」与「穿过去」。

abstract.en: Previously is what a writer says before adding: this was already true, and you may have forgotten it.
abstract.cn: previously 是作者在补充一句之前先说的：这件事早就成立，你可能已经忘了。

examples.en: The shop was previously a bank.
examples.cn: 这家店以前是一家银行。

examples.en: The room had previously been used as a storeroom.
examples.cn: 这间屋子此前曾被用作储藏室。

examples.en: As previously agreed, the meeting will start at nine.
examples.cn: 按照先前商定的，会议将在九点开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「普瑞维斯里」——previous 是「先前的」，尾巴再加一个里，就成了「先前里」，也就是以前。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ via（路）→ praevius（走在前面的）→ 英语 previous（先前的），再加副词词尾 -ly 得 previously。一般认为 previous 最早见于十七世纪，具体年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being further back along the road; the senses split by their reference point, now or a past moment, and then by a text's earlier pages.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「在路上的更后方」；义项按参照点分开，或对着现在，或对着过去的某一刻，最后是文章里更靠前的段落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller glancing back at the stretch of road already walked.
core.cn: 核心意象：行路人回头看向自己已经走过的那段路。

branches.en: an old sign still naming the shop's former business
branches.cn: 旧招牌上还写着店铺从前的营生

branches.en: a desk cleared before the new owner arrived
branches.cn: 新主人到来前就清空的桌子

branches.en: a line in a report pointing to a page above
branches.cn: 报告里指向前面某页的一行字

branches.en: a photograph taken long before the renovation
branches.cn: 装修很久之前拍的一张照片

branches.en: a footnote saying the point was already made
branches.cn: 脚注里说这一点前文已述

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place on the Latin noun for road, plus an English ending that turns the whole thing into an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示位置的拉丁前缀加拉丁语「路」这个名词，再加一个把整体变成副词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: in the manner of, at the time of

latinEntries.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；迎面而来的

definition_zh: 价格；代价；给…定价；报价
definition_en: the amount of money for which something is sold, or what must be given up to obtain something
core_image: 货架上一枚小小的价签，数字不大，却决定了谁会拿起这件商品
scene: 货架前，顾客翻过价签看背面，又把商品放回原位，转身走向更便宜的一排。The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
sceneCN: 这里 price 指「商品的售价」（第 1 个义项：出售商品所要求的金额）；句意为这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。图中可辨识物件：货架价签、翻看标签的顾客、更便宜的一排商品、被放回的外套；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 给…定价；标价（动词重音不变）

senses.title: The money asked for a good
senses.definition: the amount of money a seller asks for an item or service
senses.definitionCN: 卖方为某件商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。
senses.why: the core sense is a stated amount, which is what a price tag shows.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个被标出的金额，也就是价签所显示的内容。

senses.title: What must be given up
senses.titleCN: 为得到某物必须付出的代价
senses.definition: the cost in effort, risk or lost alternatives of obtaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而在努力、风险或放弃的其他选择上付出的代价
senses.example: The price of success was three years without weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 成功的代价是三年没有周末。
senses.why: the word extends from money to any scarce thing given up, because both are what one pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从金钱延伸到任何被放弃的稀缺之物，因为两者都是所付出的东西。

senses.title: To set a price on something
senses.definition: to decide and mark the amount to be charged for an item
senses.definitionCN: 决定并标出某项商品的收费金额
senses.example: They priced the tickets at twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把票价定为二十英镑。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into an act of assigning the amount.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转为「指派金额」的动作。

senses.title: The general level of prices
senses.definition: the average level of charges across an economy at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期一个经济体中收费的平均水平
senses.example: Prices rose faster than wages for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 有十年时间，物价涨得比工资快。
senses.why: in the plural the word often means the general level rather than one tag.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，这个词常指总体水平，而非一张价签。

senses.title: A reward offered for a capture
senses.titleCN: 为缉拿或寻回而设的赏金
senses.definition: a sum offered to anyone who finds a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 向找到某人或某物者提供的金额
senses.example: A price was put on the fugitive's head.
senses.exampleCN: 有人为这名逃犯的人头设了赏金。
senses.why: the older sense treats a reward as the amount paid for a result.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项把赏金看作「为某个结果所付的金额」。

senses.title: A quoted buying or selling rate
senses.definition: the rate at which a dealer will buy or sell in a financial market
senses.definitionCN: 交易商在金融市场愿意买进或卖出的价位
senses.example: The bond price fell after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告之后债券价格下跌。
senses.why: financial markets quote two prices, a bid and an offer, so the noun names a rate rather than a tag.
senses.whyCN: 金融市场报出买价与卖价两个价位，因此这个名词指一个比率，而非标签。

senses.title: Odds in racing or betting
senses.definition: the odds offered on a horse or outcome, expressed as a price
senses.definitionCN: 对某匹马或某个结果开出的赔率，以价位表示
senses.example: The bookmaker shortened the price on the favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 博彩商调低了热门马匹的赔率。
senses.why: betting calls odds a price because the stake buys a chance at a return.
senses.whyCN: 博彩把赔率称作 price，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

senses.title: Any scale of worth
senses.titleCN: 衡量与交换的价值尺度（抽象义）
senses.definition: the measure by which a society or person values something
senses.definitionCN: 社会或个人用来衡量某物价值的尺度
senses.example: Health has no price in the ordinary market sense.
senses.exampleCN: 健康在普通市场意义上没有价格。
senses.why: the word generalizes once value itself is what is being measured, not only goods.
senses.whyCN: 当被衡量的是价值本身而非仅商品时，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Price comes through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. It is a doublet of prize in the sense of value, but not of prize meaning an award. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。它与表示「价值」的 prize 是对偶词，但与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不是。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium covered price, value and reward, so the Latin word already contained both the commercial and the figurative seeds.
items.cn: pretium 兼指价格、价值与报酬，因此这个拉丁词已同时含商业义与比喻义的种子。

items.en: Old French pris meant the amount asked or the worth of a thing, and passed both senses to English.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 指索要的金额或某物的价值，并把这两层意思都传给英语。

items.en: English price appears in the thirteenth century; the plural came to mean the general cost of living.
items.cn: 英语 price 出现于 13 世纪；其复数后来指一般生活成本。

items.en: Prize meaning value is a variant of price; prize meaning an award came from Old French prise 'a capture', from prendre 'to take', a different root.
items.cn: 表示「价值」的 prize 是 price 的变体；表示「奖赏」的 prize 来自古法语 prise「捕获」，再上溯 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

items.en: The figurative price of success and the betting price of a horse extend the same core: something must be paid for an outcome.
items.cn: 「成功的代价」与赛马的「赔率」都延伸同一核心：为了某个结果必须付出某物。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. Latin pretium and Old French pris are well documented.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。拉丁 pretium 与古法语 pris 都有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like price or share its root but differ in sense; group two holds near terms for an amount charged.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 price 或与其同根、但意义不同的词；第二组是表示「所收金额」的近义词。

entries.definition: As value, it is a doublet of price; as an award, it descends from prendre 'to take'. Only the first sense is etymologically the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 作「价值」解时，它是 price 的对偶词；作「奖赏」解时，上溯 prendre「拿取」。只有前一义在词源上是同一个词。

entries.definition: From Latin pretiosus 'costly', built on pretium; it describes worth, not the amount charged.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pretiosus「贵重」，建于 pretium 之上；它描述价值，而非所收金额。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value'; it means to estimate worth, not to set a selling price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」；意为估算价值，而非设定售价。

entries.definition: Built on price with -y, meaning expensive; it describes the level, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 price 加 -y 构成，意为昂贵；它描述水平，而非金额本身。

entries.definition: The expense of making or obtaining something; price is what the buyer pays, and the two need not be equal.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或取得某物的支出；price 是买主所付，两者不必相等。

entries.definition: The amount a provider demands for a service; it is close to price but more common for services and fees.
entries.definitionCN: 服务提供者索要的金额；与 price 接近，但更常用于服务与费用。

entries.definition: A fixed payment for a professional service or privilege; it is a kind of price with a narrower setting.
entries.definitionCN: 为专业服务或特权支付的固定款项；它是范围更窄的一类价格。

entries.definition: The worth of something to a person; price is what is asked, while value is what is judged.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某人的价值；price 是所要之数，value 是被判断的价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pretium 'value': the same root runs through price, precious and appraise.
normal.cn: 拉丁 pretium「价值」：同一词根贯穿 price、precious 与 appraise。

normal.en: The family runs price, pricing, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、pricing、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: market price, price tag, price increase.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：市场价格、价签、价格上涨。

normal.en: The figurative sense is marked by of: the price of success, the price of silence.
normal.cn: 比喻义由 of 标出：成功的代价、沉默的代价。

normal.en: Betting uses price for odds, because a stake buys a chance at a return.
normal.cn: 博彩用 price 指赔率，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny tag that decides whether a hand reaches out or moves on.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小小的价签，决定一只手是伸出去还是走开。

abstract.en: Picture a coin placed on one side of a scale and a thing on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一边放硬币，另一边放物品。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line with a toll booth in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条终点线前面立着一个收费亭。

examples.en: The price of the ticket includes the ferry crossing.
examples.cn: 票价包含渡船费用。

examples.en: They paid a high price for ignoring the warning.
examples.cn: 他们因忽视警告付出了高昂代价。

examples.en: The dealer quoted a price for the old car.
examples.cn: 经销商为这辆旧车报了价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）」——货架上那个决定买不买的数字 → 价格、代价

root: 拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」→ 古法语 pris → 英语 price；与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不同源，但与表示「价值」的 prize 属对偶词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: a seller states what a thing costs, and that number is then read as a tag, a sacrifice, a verb, a general level, a reward, a quoted rate, betting odds, and finally any scale of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：卖方说出某物要多少钱，这个数字再被读作价签、牺牲、动词、总体水平、赏金、报价、赔率，最后是任何价值尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small tag whose number decides whether a hand reaches out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚小价签，其数字决定一只手是否伸出。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND ACT: the number on the tag, and the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 金额与动作：价签上的数字，以及把数字放上去的动作。

branches.en: SACRIFICE AND SCALE: what must be given up, and the wider measure of worth it implies.
branches.cn: 牺牲与尺度：必须放弃的东西，以及它所含的更广价值尺度。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LEVEL: prices in the plural become the cost of living.
branches.cn: 总体水平：复数的 prices 成为生活成本。

branches.en: REWARD AND QUOTE: a sum offered for a capture, and a rate quoted in a market.
branches.cn: 赏金与报价：为缉拿所设的金额，以及市场中报出的价位。

branches.en: BETTING ODDS: the stake buys a chance, so the odds are called a price.
branches.cn: 博彩赔率：赌注买到机会，因此赔率被称作价格。

intro.en: Price is a borrowed Latin noun that English has turned into a verb, an adjective and an action noun, so the family spreads in several directions.
intro.cn: price 是借入的拉丁名词，英语把它变成动词、形容词与动作名词，因此词族向多个方向展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium, pretiosus and pretiare supply price, precious, appraise and appreciate; English suffixes supply pricing, priced, pricey and priceless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium、pretiosus 与 pretiare 提供 price、precious、appraise 与 appreciate；英语后缀提供 pricing、priced、pricey 与 priceless。

items.example: The root carries both money and worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼含金钱与价值。

items.structure: Latin pretium via Old French pris
items.example: The price held steady all year.
The book is priced at twelve pounds.
The seats were pricey but comfortable.
The diary is priceless to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记对历史学者而言无价。
卖方把这套房子定价过高。

items.example: They underpriced the tickets and sold out.
items.exampleCN: 他们把票价定得过低，结果售罄。
一位估价师为这幅画估了价。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊（心）；狮群；以……为荣
definition_en: a warm feeling about one's own or another's achievement; an excessive sense of one's own importance; self-respect; a group of lions; and, as a verb, to feel proud about something one has
core_image: 胸膛往上一提，下巴微微抬起的那一瞬
scene: 毕业典礼上，主持人念到儿子的名字，母亲坐在观众席里，背一下子挺直了。Her face shone with pride as her son walked across the stage to take his diploma.
sceneCN: 这里 pride 指「自豪、骄傲」（第 1 个义项：因自己或亲近的人取得成绩而心里发亮）；句意为儿子走上台领取毕业证书时，她脸上泛着自豪的光。图中可辨识物件：毕业证书、观众席、被念到名字的学生。

pos.zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊；狮群
以……为荣（用于 pride oneself on）

derivatives.zh: 与 pride 同属古英语 prūd 词族，但不是由 pride 加后缀得来：pride 是名词，proud 是形容词，义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
由 pride 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「自负的；傲慢的」
由形容词 proud 加 -ly 构成，义为「自豪地；得意地」，与 pride 同源而词形不同

senses.title: A warm feeling about one's own or another's success
senses.definition: a feeling of deep pleasure and satisfaction that comes from what you or people close to you have done or possess
senses.definitionCN: 因自己或亲近的人所做成、所拥有的事而感到的深切愉快与满足
senses.example: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。
senses.why: The Old English noun first named the bare quality of being proud, and English kept its warmer half: the lift a person feels when something of theirs turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词最早只指「骄傲」这种性质，英语留下了它温暖的一半：当自己这边的事情做成了，人心里往上一提，这就是自豪。

senses.title: An exaggerated belief in one's own importance
senses.definition: an unreasonable feeling that you are better or more important than other people
senses.definitionCN: 毫无道理地觉得自己比别人强、比别人重要
senses.example: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。
senses.why: The same self-regard that lifts a person up can also close the ears: once the good opinion of oneself grows past what the facts support, the word slides into the vice that preachers warn against.
senses.whyCN: 同一种自我看重既能让人挺起胸，也能堵住耳朵：当一个人对自己的好评超过了事实能撑住的分量，这个词就滑向传道者所警告的那种恶。

senses.title: The respect a person keeps for themselves
senses.definition: a proper sense of one's own worth that keeps a person from doing something shameful
senses.definitionCN: 对自己价值的正当意识，使人不肯做出丢脸的事
senses.example: He had too much pride to ask for help with the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自尊心太强，不肯开口求人帮忙付房租。
senses.why: Between the warm sense and the arrogant one lies a third: pride as the floor a person refuses to sink below, the line kept even when nobody is watching.
senses.whyCN: 在「暖」和「傲」之间还有第三层：pride 是一个人拒绝再往下退的那块地板，即使没人看着也不肯越过的界线，所以是自尊。

senses.title: A group of lions living and hunting together
senses.definition: a group of lions that live and hunt together, usually led by related females
senses.definitionCN: 共同生活、共同捕猎的一群狮子，通常由有亲缘关系的母狮带领
senses.example: A pride of lions lay in the shade, waiting for the heat to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一群狮子卧在树荫里，等暑气过去。
senses.why: This sense comes from medieval hunting language, where each kind of animal was given its own company name; naming a band of lions was one entry in that list, and only this one survived in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自中世纪的狩猎用语，当时人们给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名，狮子那一栏就是 pride，而这一栏是唯一留到日常英语里的。

senses.title: To feel proud about a skill or possession of one's own
senses.definition: to feel a strong, often slightly self-satisfied pleasure about a skill, quality, or possession of one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对自己拥有的本领、品质或东西感到强烈的、常带点自得的满意
senses.example: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb inside the pattern to pride oneself on, where oneself is the person being lifted and the preposition on names the thing that does the lifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词套进 to pride oneself on 这个句式后就当动词用：oneself 是被抬起来的那个自己，介词 on 后面则是抬人的理由，也就是凭什么觉得自己了不起。

intro.en: Pride is an Old English noun built on the adjective proud, and that adjective is generally traced through French to a Late Latin word for profit; the word therefore began as a judgement of worth before it split into warm and cold senses.
intro.cn: pride 是古英语里由形容词 proud 造出的名词，而那个形容词一般认为经法语上溯到晚期拉丁语中表示「有好处」的词；所以它最初是对「有没有价值」的判断，之后才分成暖、冷两路。

items.en: The Latin verb prodesse meant to be of use or of advantage, and its stem prōd- is the base that later Romance forms are usually traced to.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 prodesse 意为「有用、有好处」，一般认为后来的罗曼语词形都追到它的词干 prōd-。

items.en: The Late Latin form prode meant useful or profitable, and in the spoken Latin of the provinces it also took on the colour of brave or worthy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 prode 意为「有用的、有利的」，在各省的口语拉丁语里又沾上了「勇敢、可敬」的色彩。

items.en: Old French prud or prod described a man who was brave and worthy, a sense still visible in the modern French preux.
items.cn: 古法语 prud、prod 形容人勇敢可敬，这层意思在今天的法语 preux 里还能看到。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective as prūd, which in Old English already meant proud, arrogant, and splendid at the same time; from it the noun prȳde was formed.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，写作古英语 prūd，当时就同时表示「骄傲的、傲慢的、华贵的」三面；名词 prȳde 正是由它造出来的。

items.en: Middle English prede or pride settled on the spelling pride, and the old single quality divided into praise-worthy self-respect and blame-worthy conceit, with the lion sense added from hunting vocabulary.
items.cn: 中古英语的 prede、pride 最终定为 pride 这个拼写，原本混在一起的性质分成值得称赞的自尊与该受责备的自负，狮群一义则从狩猎词汇补进来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective that pride was built from and the words closest to it in spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for self-regard, both deserved and inflated.
note.cn: 形近组收了 pride 借以构成的那个形容词及拼写最接近的几个词；近义组收表示自我看重的词，既有应得的，也有膨胀的。

entries.definition: Feeling pleased about one's own or another's achievements; the adjective that English used to build the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 为自己或他人的成就感到高兴的；英语正是用它造出了名词 pride。

entries.definition: Showing too high an opinion of oneself; built on the noun with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 过于自负的；由名词加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A person who is easily shocked by matters of the body; it comes from a French word for a modest woman, so the similarity is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 对身体方面的事容易大惊小怪的人；来自法语中表示「端庄女子」的词，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To push someone or something with a finger or a stick; a different word with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 用手指或棍子捅；另一个词，来源不同。

entries.definition: An unpleasant belief that one is better than everyone else.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的、认为自己高于所有人的信念。

entries.definition: The calm, serious quality of deserving respect.
entries.definitionCN: 值得尊重的沉稳庄重。

entries.definition: The good opinion a person has of their own character.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对自身品格的正面评价。

entries.definition: The pleasant feeling of having got what one wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 得到想要之物后的愉快感觉。

normalIntro.en: The noun was grown from an adjective that English borrowed from French, so the family keeps one ancient stem but two different shapes.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是从英语借自法语的形容词上长出来的，所以同族词共用一个古老词干，却有两种不同词形。

normal.en: Pride is the noun and proud is the adjective: English formed prȳde from prūd, which is why the two never look alike today.
normal.cn: pride 是名词，proud 是形容词：古英语从 prūd 造出 prȳde，所以今天两者词形完全不同。

normal.en: The -ful in prideful turns the noun into an adjective, the same -ful that appears in careful and hopeful.
normal.cn: prideful 里的 -ful 把名词变成形容词，和 careful、hopeful 里的 -ful 是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Swallow one's pride is a picture of forcing something down the throat: the feeling is still there, only hidden.
normal.cn: swallow one's pride 是一幅把东西硬咽下去的画：情绪还在，只是藏起来了。

normal.en: A pride of lions follows the old hunting habit of giving every kind of animal its own collective name.
normal.cn: a pride of lions 沿用古老的狩猎习惯：给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名。

normal.en: Pride oneself on needs the reflexive pronoun because the one who boasts is also the one being lifted.
normal.cn: pride oneself on 必须带反身代词，因为夸人的和被抬高的其实是同一个。

abstract.en: One word covers a mother's lifted chin and a tyrant's closed ears, because both are the same self looking at itself.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着母亲抬起的下巴和暴君堵住的耳朵，因为两者都是「自我在看自己」。

abstract.en: Pride as dignity is pride turned inward and kept quiet; pride as conceit is the same force turned outward and made loud.
abstract.cn: 作为尊严的 pride 向内收着、不出声；作为自负的 pride 是同一股力向外放、喊得很响。

abstract.en: The lion sense survives as a fossil: a whole medieval habit of naming animal groups, kept alive by one entry.
abstract.cn: 狮群义像一块化石：中世纪给动物群体起名的一整套习惯，只靠这一条留了下来。

examples.en: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
examples.cn: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。

examples.en: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
examples.cn: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。

examples.en: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
examples.cn: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑赖德」——一股气从胸口扑上来，赖着不走，那就是 pride。

root: 古英语 prȳde（骄傲）由 prūd（骄傲的）加名词词尾构成，prūd 一般认为借自古法语 prud、prod，可上溯到晚期拉丁语 prode（有用的、有利的），出自拉丁语 prodesse（有益）。同源的形容词 proud 保留了另一支词形。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a self looking at itself with approval; the senses divide into the warm feeling, the cold excess, the line of self-respect, the lion group, and the verb of taking pride in something.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「自我满意地看着自己」；义项由此分出温暖的自豪、过头的自负、守住的尊严、狮群，以及表示「以……为荣」的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest lifting and a chin rising for a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口往上一提，下巴微微一抬的那一瞬。

branches.en: a mother's back straightening at a ceremony
branches.cn: 典礼上母亲把背挺直的一瞬

branches.en: a man who will not say sorry
branches.cn: 一个死活不肯道歉的人

branches.en: a hand pushing away a coin offered in pity
branches.cn: 一只推开怜悯施舍的手

branches.en: tawny bodies resting in tall grass
branches.cn: 高草里卧着的一群黄褐色身影

branches.en: a chef boasting about his own knife work
branches.cn: 厨师夸自己的刀工

intro.en: The word is an Old English noun grown from a borrowed adjective, and the eight pieces below trace that adjective back through French to a Latin word of profit.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语里从借来的形容词长成的名词，下面八条把它经由法语一路追回拉丁语中表示「有好处」的词。

latinIntro.en: A Late Latin adjective of profit stands behind the French form that English borrowed, so a Latin cognate does exist here, although the link is indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 英语借来的法语词形背后有晚期拉丁语中表示「有好处」的形容词，所以这个词确有拉丁同族，只是关系是间接的。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 神父；牧师；祭司；教士
definition_en: an ordained religious minister, especially a Catholic or Anglican one, or an official who performs sacred rites in another religion
core_image: 祭坛前系着圣带、转过身来的黑袍身影
scene: 清晨的老教堂里，木门刚开，长椅上还留着昨夜的凉气，一位穿黑袍的人站在祭坛前把圣带系好。The priest turned from the altar and greeted the first old woman who came in from the cold.
sceneCN: 这里 priest 指「神父」（第 1 个义项：天主教会中主持弥撒、听告解的圣职人员）；句意为神父从祭坛前转过身，向第一位进来避寒的老妇人问安。图中可辨识物件：祭坛、圣带、教堂长椅。

derivatives.zh: 由 priest 加抽象名词后缀 -hood 构成，义为「神职；司铎身份；全体神职人员」
由 priest 加表示女性的后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女祭司」
由 priest 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「神职人员的；像教士的」

senses.title: An ordained minister of the Catholic or Orthodox Church
senses.definition: a man ordained in the Roman Catholic or Orthodox Church to celebrate Mass and to hear confession
senses.definitionCN: 在天主教或东正教会中受圣职、可以主持弥撒并听告解的男子
senses.example: The priest listened to her confession for nearly an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 神父听了她近一个小时的告解。
senses.why: Greek presbyteros meant an elder of the community, and the western church kept that title for the man who stands at the altar on the people's behalf; the everyday English name for him is this word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 presbyteros 本是「团体中的长老」，西方教会把这个称号留给代表众人站在祭坛前的人，英语里对这个人最常用的称呼就是 priest。

senses.title: An ordained minister in Anglican and similar churches
senses.definition: a member of the clergy in the Church of England and churches of similar order, ranking below a bishop
senses.definitionCN: 英国国教会及同类教会中的圣职人员，位次低于主教
senses.example: The priest read the notices and then blessed the small congregation.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师念完通告，随后为这一小群会众祝福。
senses.why: Where the church kept the old ladder of deacon, priest and bishop, the middle rung kept the old name too, so an Anglican clergyman is a priest rather than a minister.
senses.whyCN: 凡保留了「会吏—司铎—主教」这套旧阶梯的教会，中间那一级也保留了旧名，所以圣公会的圣职人员叫 priest，而不叫 minister。

senses.title: An official who offers sacrifice in another religion
senses.definition: a person who performs sacred rites and offers sacrifice in a non-Christian or ancient religion
senses.definitionCN: 在非基督教或古代宗教中主持圣事、献祭的人
senses.example: A priest lit the fire before the stone image at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时，祭司在石像前点起了火。
senses.why: The word was never limited to one faith: any religion that sets aside a person to handle sacrifice and ritual gets the same English label, because the job, not the creed, is what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从未只属于一种信仰：任何宗教只要专门设一个人来管献祭与仪式，英语都用同一个词，因为这个词命名的是那份职责，而不是教义。

senses.title: A clergyman as a familiar figure in a community
senses.definition: a member of the clergy spoken of informally as a local figure, especially one serving a village, a parish, or a hospital
senses.definitionCN: 对神职人员的口语统称，尤指在村庄、堂区或医院里服务的那一位
senses.example: The village priest buried three generations of the same family.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的教士安葬过同一家族的三代人。
senses.why: Once a community has one such man who baptizes, marries and buries its people, the word stops describing an office and starts naming a familiar neighbour, which is this looser fourth sense.
senses.whyCN: 当一个社区里总有这么一个人为孩子洗礼、为新人证婚、为逝者下葬，这个词就不再只是在说一个职衔，而是在说一位熟悉的邻居，这就是更宽松的第四义。

intro.en: Priest goes back to a Greek word for an older man: the church took the word for a community elder, Latin passed it on, and the Germanic languages borrowed it early enough to wear its edges smooth.
intro.cn: priest 的源头是希腊语中表示「年长者」的词：教会借它指团体里的长老，拉丁语再往下传，日耳曼诸语借得早，把词形磨得很圆。

items.en: The Greek noun presbys meant an old man or an elder, someone whose age gave him standing in the group.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 presbys 指老人、长者，年岁让他在群体里有发言的分量。

items.en: Its comparative presbyteros meant older, and the early Greek-speaking church used it for the elders who governed a congregation.
items.cn: 它的比较级 presbyteros 意为「较年长的」，早期讲希腊语的教会用它指管理会众的长老。

items.en: Latin took the title as presbyter, an elder of the church, and kept it for the second order of clergy below the bishop.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个称号接过去写作 presbyter，指教会中的长老，后来专指低于主教的第二级圣职人员。

items.en: The Germanic peoples borrowed the spoken Latin form at an early date; Old English has prēost, with the middle consonants worn down, and the word was in use long before the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 日耳曼各族很早就借用了拉丁语的口语词形；古英语里已有 prēost，中间几个辅音被磨掉，这个词在诺曼征服之前很久就在用了。

items.en: Middle English preost became modern priest, and Latin presbyter was later borrowed a second time as a learned word, so priest and presbyter are one root reached by two roads.
items.cn: 中古英语 preost 变成现代英语 priest；后来拉丁语 presbyter 又被当作学术词再借一次，所以 priest 与 presbyter 是同一个词根走了两条路。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek and Latin forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers the other English names for a religious minister.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一词根的希腊语、拉丁语词形展开；近义组收英语里对宗教圣职人员的其他称呼。

entries.definition: An elder of the early church; the Latin form was borrowed into English a second time as a learned term.
entries.definitionCN: 早期教会中的长老；这个拉丁词形后来被当作学术词再次借入英语。

entries.definition: The body of elders of a church, or the part of a church reserved for the clergy.
entries.definitionCN: 教会的长老团，或教堂中供圣职人员使用的区域。

entries.definition: Belonging to a church governed by elders rather than bishops.
entries.definitionCN: 属于由长老而非主教治理的教会的。

entries.definition: A woman who performs sacred rites, formed by adding the feminine suffix -ess.
entries.definitionCN: 主持圣事的女性，由加女性后缀 -ess 构成。

entries.definition: A member of the clergy, especially in a Protestant church.
entries.definitionCN: 圣职人员，尤指新教教会的。

entries.definition: A man who has been ordained for religious duties.
entries.definitionCN: 受圣职、担任宗教职务的男子。

entries.definition: A minister who cares for a particular congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 照管某个会众的牧师。

entries.definition: A priest in charge of a parish in the Church of England.
entries.definitionCN: 英国国教会中主管一个堂区的牧师。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek title for an elder that travelled through Latin into Old English, and its family still splits into the churchly and the scholarly branch.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语对长者的称呼，经拉丁语进入古英语，它的同族至今分成教会用语与学术用语两支。

normal.en: Presbyteros in Greek means an older man, so a priest began as the elder of a group rather than a man with a special power.
normal.cn: 希腊语 presbyteros 意为「较年长的人」，所以 priest 最初是团体里的长者，而不是拥有特殊法力的人。

normal.en: The same root gives presbyter, presbytery and Presbyterian, all of them about elders rather than altars.
normal.cn: 同一个词根给出 presbyter、presbytery 与 Presbyterian，讲的都是长老而不是祭坛。

normal.en: Old English prēost borrowed the spoken Latin form early, which is why the spelling is so far from presbyter.
normal.cn: 古英语 prēost 很早就借了口语词形，所以拼写和 presbyter 差得很远。

normal.en: The -hood in priesthood marks a state or office, as it does in childhood and brotherhood.
normal.cn: priesthood 里的 -hood 表示身份或状态，和 childhood、brotherhood 一样。

normal.en: The -ess in priestess marks a female counterpart, the same ending as in actress and goddess.
normal.cn: priestess 里的 -ess 表示女性对应者，和 actress、goddess 用法相同。

abstract.en: The word travels from age to office: first an old man, then the elder of a congregation, then the man at the altar.
abstract.cn: 这个词从年岁走向职分：先是老人，再是会众的长老，最后是站在祭坛前的人。

abstract.en: One root reaches English twice, once worn smooth as priest and once kept sharp as presbyter, like a coin and its proof.
abstract.cn: 一个词根两次抵达英语，一次磨圆成 priest，一次保持原样成 presbyter，像流通的硬币与它的样币。

abstract.en: A priest is defined by standing in for others, which is why the same word serves faiths that share no creed.
abstract.cn: priest 的关键是替别人站到前面，所以这个词能同时服务彼此毫无共同教义的宗教。

examples.en: The priest turned from the altar to greet the first visitor.
examples.cn: 神父从祭坛前转过身，向第一位来客问安。

examples.en: Her grandfather was a Catholic priest in a small mountain parish.
examples.cn: 她的祖父是山区小堂区的一位天主教神父。

examples.en: In the temple, a priest lit the fire before the stone image.
examples.cn: 庙里，祭司在石像前点起了火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里斯特」——听着像「仆里侍」：在祭坛边侍奉的人，就是 priest。

root: 希腊语 presbys（老人）→ 比较级 presbyteros（较年长的、长老）→ 拉丁语 presbyter（教会长老）→ 日耳曼语早借，古英语 prēost → 现代英语 priest。后来拉丁语 presbyter 又被直接再借一次，成为学术同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an elder who stands for the group before the sacred; the senses divide by which church is speaking, then widen to any officiant of sacrifice and to the familiar local clergyman.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「替众人站到神圣面前的年长者」；义项按说话的教会分开，再扩到任何主持献祭的人，最后落到社区里那位熟悉的教士。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in dark robes turning from the altar toward the people.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿深色长袍的身影从祭坛前转过身，面向众人。

branches.en: a black cassock turning from the altar
branches.cn: 黑袍从祭坛前转过身

branches.en: a vicar reading notices after the service
branches.cn: 礼拜结束后宣读通告的牧师

branches.en: a fire lit before a stone image
branches.cn: 石像前燃起的火

branches.en: a familiar figure at every village burial
branches.cn: 每场乡村葬礼上都出现的身影

branches.en: the same man at the altar and at the graveside
branches.cn: 同一个人在祭坛前，也在墓旁

intro.en: The word is a Greek comparative of age, its Latin church title, the worn Old English borrowing, and the English endings that name the office and its female counterpart.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语中表示年岁的比较级、拉丁语的教会称号、磨圆的古英语借词，以及命名职分与女性对应者的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Greek title entered Latin as presbyter and stayed in church use, so a Latin cognate is well recorded even though English took the word by an older spoken route.
latinIntro.cn: 这个希腊称号进入拉丁语后写作 presbyter 并一直在教会里使用，所以拉丁同族有明确记录，只是英语走的是更早的口语路径。

items.meaning: church elder, priest of the second order

latinEntries.meaning: the body of elders, the place reserved for them
latinEntries.meaningCN: 长老团；长老所在的区域

definition_zh: 主要地；首要地；首先
definition_en: mainly, above all other things or purposes
core_image: 一栋房子的正门，旁边还有几扇小侧门
scene: 这座城市的经济靠港口，其他行业规模都小得多。The city's economy is primarily dependent on the port.
sceneCN: 这里指首要、占主导（第 1 个义项：主要地）；句意为这座城市的经济主要依赖港口；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Mainly
senses.definition: for the most part, more than any other thing
senses.definitionCN: 大部分情况下，超过任何其他事物
senses.example: The book is primarily about language.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书主要讲语言。
senses.why: The word ranks one element above the rest without denying that others exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把某一要素排在其余之上，却不否认其余要素存在。

senses.title: First in responsibility
senses.definition: used of the person or body with the main duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于承担主要职责的人或机构
senses.example: The committee is primarily responsible for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对安全负主要责任。
senses.why: Here the word concerns rank of obligation, not frequency or quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这里它说的是责任的等级，而不是频率或数量。

senses.title: Primarily because
senses.definition: used to name the main reason among several
senses.definitionCN: 用来在多个原因中指出主要那一个
senses.example: He resigned primarily because of ill health.
senses.exampleCN: 他辞职主要是因为健康不佳。
senses.why: The causal pattern admits other reasons while naming the dominant one.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果句式承认还有其他原因，同时点出主导原因。

senses.title: Primarily for a purpose
senses.definition: of a thing, intended first of all for one use
senses.definitionCN: 指某物的首要用途
senses.example: The land is used primarily for farming.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地主要用于耕作。
senses.why: The word identifies the main function, leaving other uses as secondary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指出主要功能，把其他用途留作次要。

senses.title: Primarily designed to
senses.definition: used before a verb of design or purpose to state the main aim
senses.definitionCN: 放在设计或目的动词前，说明主要目标
senses.example: The tool is primarily designed to cut wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这件工具的首要设计目的是切木头。
senses.why: Technical descriptions use the word to separate the intended function from incidental ones.
senses.whyCN: 技术说明用它把预期功能与附带功能分开。

senses.title: Primarily aimed at
senses.definition: of a course or product, intended mainly for one group
senses.definitionCN: 指课程或产品主要面向某一群体
senses.example: The programme is primarily aimed at beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目主要面向初学者。
senses.why: The pattern states the target audience and implies that others are not the main concern.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式说明目标受众，并暗示其他人不是主要考虑。

senses.title: Formal register for mainly
senses.definition: in formal prose, a heavier alternative to mainly
senses.definitionCN: 在正式散文中，作为「主要」的较重替代
senses.example: The decline is primarily due to changes in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 这一下降主要归因于需求变化。
senses.why: Formal writing prefers the word when the claim carries weight in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 当论断在论证中有分量时，正式文字更偏爱这个词。

senses.title: Primarily concerned with
senses.definition: used of a field or text, focused on one subject above others
senses.definitionCN: 指某领域或文本把某一主题置于其他之上
senses.example: The chapter is primarily concerned with ethics.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章主要关注伦理问题。
senses.why: The phrase describes the centre of attention, often in academic summaries.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语描述注意力的中心，常用于学术摘要。

intro.en: Primarily comes from the Latin adjective for first in rank, through English primary, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「第一等级」的形容词，经英语形容词「首要的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adjective primus means first in order or rank.
items.cn: 形容词意为「在次序或等级上第一的」。

items.en: The adjective primarius means of the first rank or chief.
items.cn: 形容词意为「第一等级的、首要的」。

items.en: English primary comes through French and means first in importance as well as first in order.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，既指次序最先，也指重要性居首。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage ranks importance and purpose rather than strict temporal order.
items.cn: 现代用法排的是重要性与目的，而不是严格的时间先后。

items.en: The adverb settles in formal and technical prose as a stronger mainly.
items.cn: 这个副词在正式与技术散文中定型，语气比「主要地」更重。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin first-rank family; the second group contrasts main importance with leading rank or plain majority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「第一等级」词族；第二组对照「主要重要性」与「首领地位」或「单纯多数」。

entries.definition: First in importance or order; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或次序上第一的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The state of being first in rank or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 在等级或权威上居首的状态。

entries.definition: First in quality or importance; also the period of greatest strength.
entries.definitionCN: 在质量或重要性上居首；也指最强盛的时期。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 属于最早或最基础层面的。

entries.definition: For the most part; the plainer everyday counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分情况下；更朴素的日常对应词。

entries.definition: Above all others, often ranking rather than measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，常偏重等级而非数量。

entries.definition: To a great extent, often of proportions.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上，常指比例。

entries.definition: Chiefly, with a heavier formal and institutional tone.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，带更重的正式与机构语气。

entries.definition: More than everything else, with clear ranking.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，带明确的排序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-rank family and the real split between main importance and leading rank.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「第一等级」词族，并区分「主要重要性」与「首领地位」。

normal.en: The root means first, so the word puts one item at the front of the line.
normal.cn: 词根意为「第一」，所以它把某一项排到队伍最前。

normal.en: Primarily responsible is about duty, not frequency.
normal.cn: 「负主要责任」说的是职责，不是频率。

normal.en: Primarily because names the leading reason and lets the others stand behind it.
normal.cn: 「主要因为」点出主导原因，让其他原因站在后面。

normal.en: Primarily aimed at identifies the audience the maker had in mind.
normal.cn: 「主要面向」指明制作者心里的受众。

normal.en: Formal prose uses it where mainly would sound too light for the claim.
normal.cn: 正式散文用它，因为「主要」对这份论断来说太轻。

abstract.en: Main importance is a ranking, and a ranking is a decision about what comes first.
abstract.cn: 主要性是一种排序，而排序就是决定什么排在最前。

abstract.en: A main door does not make the side doors unreal; it only decides where visitors enter.
abstract.cn: 正门并不让侧门变得不存在，它只决定客人从哪里进。

abstract.en: The word is a quiet way of saying that one reason outranks the rest.
abstract.cn: 这个词是安静地说：有一个理由压过其余。

examples.en: The region is primarily agricultural.
examples.cn: 这个地区主要从事农业。

examples.en: The delay was primarily caused by the weather.
examples.cn: 延误主要是天气造成的。

examples.en: The course is primarily intended for new staff.
examples.cn: 这门课程主要面向新员工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普赖么瑞利」——排在第一排，主要就它

root: 拉丁语形容词「第一的」构成「第一等级的、首要的」，英语经法语借入形容词「主要的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate main importance, first responsibility, leading reason, main purpose, primary design aim, target audience, formal register and academic focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理主要重要性、首要责任、主导原因、主要用途、首要设计目的、目标受众、正式语域，以及学术关注点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front door of a house, with several smaller side doors beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋房子的正门，旁边还有几扇小侧门。

branches.en: THE MAIN ELEMENT: more than any other thing.
branches.cn: 主要要素：超过任何其他事物。

branches.en: THE LEADING CLAIM: first responsibility and the dominant reason.
branches.cn: 领先的主张：首要责任与主导原因。

branches.en: THE INTENDED USE: main function and primary design aim.
branches.cn: 预期用途：主要功能与首要设计目的。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE: the group the thing is mainly for.
branches.cn: 受众：该事物主要面向的群体。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CENTRE: heavier register and the focus of a field or text.
branches.cn: 正式中心：更重的语域，以及领域或文本的关注点。

intro.en: Primarily is a Latin first-adjective, its rank adjective, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「第一」形容词、表等级的形容词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The first word builds an adjective of first rank, and English draws primary, primacy and prime from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「第一」的词构成「第一等级」的形容词，英语从同一词干取得「主要的」「首要地位」与「首要的」。

items.example: The adjective is the simple ranking word behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族背后最简单的排序词。

items.example: The suffix builds an adjective of rank.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表等级的形容词。

items.example: The adjective names those who stand at the head.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指站在最前面的人。

items.example: English keeps both the ranking and the early-stage senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留「排序」与「早期阶段」两条义。

items.example: The noun names the position rather than the quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名位置，而不是性质。

items.example: The short form covers both rank and peak time.
items.exampleCN: 短形式同时覆盖等级与巅峰时期。

items.example: Another branch stresses earliness rather than rank.
items.exampleCN: 另一分支强调「最早」，而不是等级。

items.example: The suffix turns primary into a ranking adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成排序副词。

items.example: The adverb ranks importance in a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词在整句范围内排定重要性。

definition_zh: 主要的；首要的；最初的；初级的；原生的；（美国）初选
definition_en: first in importance, order, or development; basic rather than derived
core_image: 一排门中最先打开的那一扇，所有人从这里进入
scene: 急救现场，医生先检查呼吸、出血与意识。Her primary check covered breathing, bleeding and awareness, and everything else waited until those three were answered.
sceneCN: 这里 primary 是「首要的、第一位的」（第 1 个义项：在重要性上排第一）；句意：她的首要检查覆盖呼吸、出血和意识，其余项目都等这三项有答案之后才做。图中可辨识物件：急救包、担架、监护仪、手电筒、评估表；对应第 1 个义项。

初选；初级选举；（鸟）初级飞羽

senses.title: First in importance
senses.definition: more important than all others
senses.definitionCN: 比其余一切更重要
senses.example: Safety is our primary concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们的首要关切。
senses.why: Latin primarius means 'of the first rank'. The word ranks things: one item is placed in the first position, and the others are measured against it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 primarius 意为“第一等的”。这个词给事物排名：一项被放到第一位，其余都以它为参照。

senses.title: First in order or time
senses.definition: coming first in a sequence or process
senses.definitionCN: 在序列或过程中最先出现
senses.example: The primary stage of the reaction takes seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 反应的初始阶段只需几秒。
senses.why: Order and importance borrow the same image. What comes first in time is often what must be dealt with first, so sequence slides into priority.
senses.whyCN: 次序与重要性借用同一意象。时间上最先的，往往也是必须先处理的，于是序列滑向优先。

senses.title: Basic or elementary
senses.definition: of the first level of education or skill
senses.definitionCN: 教育或技能的第一层
senses.example: Children learn to read in primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在小学学习阅读。
senses.why: Primary education is the first tier, before secondary. The word names a floor of a building rather than a value judgment.
senses.whyCN: 初等教育是第二级之前的第一层。这个词命名建筑的一层楼，而非价值判断。

senses.title: Chief or main
senses.definition: the main or principal part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的主要或主体部分
senses.example: The primary cause was a failed valve.
senses.exampleCN: 主要原因是阀门失效。
senses.why: Here primary is close to principal: it picks out the leading element in an explanation. The two words share a root but differ in role.
senses.whyCN: 这里 primary 接近 principal：它挑出解释中的主导要素。两词共享词根，但角色不同。

senses.title: Original, not derived
senses.definition: of a source or record, created at the time, not based on another
senses.definitionCN: 来源或记录在当时产生，而非依据他物
senses.example: Historians prefer primary sources such as letters.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家偏爱书信这类原始资料。
senses.why: Research divides evidence into first-hand and second-hand. A primary source is the earliest layer; everything else is commentary on it.
senses.whyCN: 研究把证据分为第一手与第二手。原始资料是最早的一层，其余都是对它的评论。

senses.title: A US primary election
senses.definition: a state election in which voters choose party candidates
senses.definitionCN: 选民在其中选出政党候选人的州级选举
senses.example: She won the New Hampshire primary.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢下了新罕布什尔州初选。
senses.why: American politics uses the noun for the first screening election in a campaign. The word keeps its 'first stage' sense: the primary precedes the general election.
senses.whyCN: 美国政治用这个名词指竞选中的第一场筛选性选举。它保留“第一阶段”义：初选在普选之前。

senses.title: A primary feather
senses.definition: one of the flight feathers on the outer part of a bird's wing
senses.definitionCN: 鸟翼外侧的飞行羽毛
senses.example: The hawk's primaries spread wide in flight.
senses.exampleCN: 猎鹰飞行时初级飞羽大张。
senses.why: Ornithology numbers feathers from the leading edge outward. The primaries are the first flight feathers, so the word's ordinal sense becomes anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 鸟类学从翼前缘向外编号。初级飞羽是最先的飞行羽毛，于是序数义变成解剖名。

senses.title: First in a chemical chain
senses.definition: of a carbon atom or compound, attached to one other carbon group
senses.definitionCN: 碳原子或化合物只与一个其他碳基相连
senses.example: Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes.
senses.exampleCN: 伯醇氧化成醛。
senses.why: Chemistry labels structures by position in a chain: primary, secondary, tertiary. The naming is ordinal, borrowed straight from the Latin 'first rank'.
senses.whyCN: 化学按链上的位置标记结构：伯、仲、叔。命名是序数性的，直接借自拉丁语“第一等”。

senses.title: One of the primary colors
senses.definition: in color theory, a color from which others can be mixed
senses.definitionCN: 色彩理论中可混合出其他颜色的基色
senses.example: Red, blue, and yellow are primary colors in painting.
senses.exampleCN: 在绘画中，红、蓝、黄是三原色。
senses.why: Color theory treats some hues as underived: they cannot be produced by mixing the others. Primary here means 'not made from anything else', the root sense of primus.
senses.whyCN: 色彩理论把某些色相视为不可再分：它们不能由其他颜色混合产生。这里 primary 意为“不是由别物制成”，是 primus 的根本义。

intro.en: Primary comes straight from Latin primarius, 'of the first rank', built on primus 'first'. English uses it for rank, for sequence, for schooling, and for anything that is not derived from something else.
intro.cn: primary 直接来自拉丁语 primarius“第一等的”，建立在 primus“第一”之上。英语用它表等级、次序、学校教育，以及任何不是由他物派生的事物。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'first in order, original, principal'.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“次序第一、原始的、主要的”。

items.en: From Latin primarius 'of the first rank or quality', from primus 'first'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 primarius“第一等或第一品质的”，源出 primus“第一”。

items.en: primus is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind prime, prior, and prince. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: primus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 prime、prior、prince。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The educational sense 'elementary' and the logical sense 'original, not derived' become established.
items.cn: 教育义“初级的”与逻辑义“原始的、非派生的”确立。

items.en: The noun primary for a direct nominating election appears in American politics.
items.cn: 名词 primary 指直接提名选举，出现在美国政治中。

items.en: Modern English spreads the word across medicine, chemistry, biology, and color theory, always keeping the ordinal core.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词铺到医学、化学、生物学与色彩理论，始终保留序数核心。

note.en: The first group shares the primus stem; the second is about adjectives that also mean chief or first.
note.cn: 第一组共享 primus 词干，第二组看同样表示“首要”或“第一”的形容词。

entries.definition: mainly; chiefly. It is primary plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；首要地。它是 primary 加 -ly。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank. It comes from Latin primatus.
entries.definitionCN: 首位；优先。来自拉丁语 primatus。

entries.definition: first in rank or quality; also a peak state. It shares primus directly.
entries.definitionCN: 第一等的；鼎盛状态。它直接共享 primus。

entries.definition: first in importance. It is close to primary sense 1 but is not used for stages or schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 重要性第一的。它接近 primary 第 1 义，但不用于阶段或教育。

entries.definition: at the very beginning. It marks sequence only, not rank.
entries.definitionCN: 在最开始的。它只标记次序，不标记等级。

entries.definition: of the simplest level. It matches the schooling sense but not the 'chief' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 最简层次的。它对应教育义，不对应“首要”义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin primus 'first', the primarius rank word, the primary/principal pair, and the primary source idea.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 primus“第一”、primarius 的等级义、primary 与 principal 这对词，以及“原始资料”概念。

normal.en: Primus means 'first'. Everything primary is first in some line: rank, time, school, or origin.
normal.cn: primus 意为“第一”。一切 primary 都在某条线上第一：等级、时间、学校或起源。

normal.en: Primary vs principal: both mean chief, but only primary is used for stages, schools, and sources.
normal.cn: primary 与 principal：两者都指首要，但只有 primary 用于阶段、学校与资料。

normal.en: Primary source is first-hand evidence; secondary source is commentary on it.
normal.cn: 原始资料是第一手证据；二手资料是对它的评论。

normal.en: Primary school is the first tier of schooling, not a school that is 'more important' than others.
normal.cn: 小学是教育的第一层，不是“比别的学校更重要”的学校。

normal.en: In chemistry, primary, secondary, and tertiary are positions on a carbon chain, numbered from the end.
normal.cn: 化学中，伯、仲、叔是碳链上的位置，从末端编号。

abstract.en: Priority is a spatial metaphor: we place one thing at the front of a line and call it first.
abstract.cn: 优先是一种空间隐喻：我们把一件事放到队伍最前，称它为第一。

abstract.en: The first is not always the best: primary means earliest, and earliest often means simplest.
abstract.cn: 最先的未必最好：primary 意为最早，而最早往往意味着最简单。

abstract.en: A primary source is powerful because it has not yet been interpreted; it is the world before commentary.
abstract.cn: 原始资料之所以有力，是因为它尚未被解释；它是评论之前的世界。

examples.en: Public safety is the primary goal of the policy.
examples.cn: 公共安全是这项政策的首要目标。

examples.en: The study relies on primary sources from the period.
examples.cn: 这项研究依赖该时期的一手资料。

examples.en: He won the primary by a narrow margin.
examples.cn: 他以微弱优势赢得初选。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来马瑞”——扑过来的马群里，第一匹最显眼 → primary 首要的、第一的

root: 拉丁语 primarius“第一等的”，源出 primus“第一”；更早为原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”。同族有 prime、prior、prince。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of primary, all ordinal: first in rank, in time, in school, in evidence, in a chemical chain, or in a color system. The word always places something at the head of a line.
sensesIntro.cn: primary 的九个义项都是序数性的：在等级、时间、学校、证据、化学链或颜色系统中排第一。这个词总是把某物放在一条线的头部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first position at the head of a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线最前端的第一位置。

branches.en: RANK: the most important item is placed first and the rest measured against it.
branches.cn: 等级：最重要的项被放在第一，其余以它为参照。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: the first stage in time, including the first election of a campaign.
branches.cn: 次序：时间上的第一阶段，包括竞选的第一场选举。

branches.en: SCHOOL: the first tier of education, basic rather than advanced.
branches.cn: 学校：教育的第一层，基础而非高级。

branches.en: ORIGIN: first-hand evidence and underived colors are not made from anything else.
branches.cn: 起源：第一手证据与不可再分的原色不是由他物制成。

branches.en: ANATOMY AND CHEMISTRY: the ordinal sense becomes naming for leading feathers and chain positions.
branches.cn: 解剖与化学：序数义变成对前缘飞羽与链上位置的命名。

intro.en: Primary is an adjective and a noun. English adds -ly and -cy, and the primus root also gives prime, primer, and prince.
intro.cn: primary 既是形容词也是名词。英语加 -ly 与 -cy，primus 词根还生成 prime、primer、prince。

latinIntro.en: Latin primarius 'of the first rank' and primus 'first' sit beside primatus 'first place' and principium 'beginning'. The family is about ordinal priority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primarius“第一等”与 primus“第一”旁边是 primatus“首位”与 principium“开端”。这个词族关乎序数优先。

items.meaning: the state of being first in rank or importance
first in rank; the best years; a prime number
items.meaningCN: 第一等的；鼎盛期；质数（同源词）

items.meaning: a royal ruler; a leading figure
chief; a school head; a sum of money
items.meaningCN: 主要的；校长；本金（同源，义不同）
